frozen_inputs.context:
--- Article 1: Untitled article
Category: LMS
LMS

How to login to LMS

1. Login

Type lms.amref.ac.ke into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer, Opera Mini) or search Google for "lms amref"

Or

2. At the top right of the homepage, upon visiting lms.amref.ac.ke, click 'Login/Register'.

3. In the pop-up window, click the "Use your Amref email address to sign in" button.

4. You will be redirected to the AMREF email login page.

will be redirected to the AMREF email login page.

You will be asked to enter your email address and password for your Amref

account before being taken to the dashboard, as shown in the photos below

5. Choose the course

On the left navigation tool of the dashboard, navigate to "My courses" and pick the course for which you wish to study, in this example, "induction module.".

Happy Learning!
Source: 
---
--- Article 2: Untitled article
Category: LMS
LMS

Student Email; Mcampus Email; Cooporate Email; Official Email

Student Email

Students have access to cooperate emails that have been created for them to use to access campus resources.

Before using the email, it needs to be ACTIVATED. Logging in = ACTIVATION

The email format is: firstname . lastname @mcampus.amref.ac.ke

For example: test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke

The password is: sent on email

campus.amref.ac.ke

The password is: sent on email

The details to access this email are individually sent to each student. The communication contains their corporate / University email address and the password for their account.

The email account has two-step verification enabled so one has to input their phone number where a code will be sent to so as to complete the login process

To access the email, on the LMS under Student Services, select Student Email
Source:

warmups_excluded.question: How do I log in to the LMS?
warmups_excluded.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — LMS login uses your Amref email account, so once that's working the rest is quick.

**Logging in to the LMS**

1. **Open the LMS.** Type `lms.amref.ac.ke` into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini all work), or search Google for "lms amref" and follow the result.
2. **Click 'Login/Register'** at the top right of the homepage — this is the entry point rather than typing credentials on the front page.
3. **In the pop-up window, click "Use your Amref email address to sign in."** The LMS doesn't hold a separate password; it hands sign-in over to your Amref email account.
4. **Enter your Amref email address and password** on the AMREF email login page you're redirected to. Your email follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your corporate/University email details.
5. **Complete the two-step verification.** The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for a phone number where a code will be sent — enter that code to finish signing in. Once verified, you land on your LMS dashboard.
6. **Open your course.** On the left navigation tool of the dashboard, go to **"My courses"** and pick the course you want to study — for example, "Induction module."

The screenshots below show these login pages so you can match what's on your screen.

**A couple of things worth knowing:**

- If you've never signed in to your Amref email before, that first login *is* the activation of the account — so if the email password has never been used, expect to be prompted to set things up before you reach the dashboard.
- You can also reach your Amref email from within the LMS: under **Student Services**, select **Student Email**.

If the sign-in still fails after this — for instance, you never received the email with your address and password — the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke can retrieve or reset those credentials for you.

*Sources: Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — "How to login to LMS" (LMS category) and "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category).*

Your address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your corporate/University email details.

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Getting locked out of the portal is annoying, but the reset is a quick self-service process — here's how to do it from start to finish.

**Before you begin:** you'll need access to your Amref student email address and the phone number registered on your student record, because the reset verifies both.

1. Open the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen — this starts the self-service reset instead of a manual request.
2. Enter your **Amref student email** and the **characters displayed** on the screen. The characters are a security check that confirms a real person is making the request.
3. Enter your **phone number**, then key in the **code sent to you via text**. This is the step that proves the account is yours, so make sure your phone is with you and has network coverage.
4. **Type your new password and confirm it**, then click **Finish**.
5. Return to the portal and **log in with your student email and your new password** — a successful login confirms the reset worked.

**Your new password must meet these rules, or it will be rejected:**

- **Length:** a minimum of **10 characters**.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

The screenshots below show the reset screens so you can match what you're seeing on your own device.

One thing worth knowing: since the reset is delivered to your student email and phone, you'll need your student email to be active. Your student email follows the format *firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke*, and logging into it for the first time is what activates it — the address and initial password are sent to you individually. If the text code never arrives or the phone number on file isn't yours anymore, that part isn't something you can fix from the portal yourself, so raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources:**

- Student Portal — https://students.amref.ac.ke/

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this — Microsoft Authenticator is what gives your AmIU Microsoft 365 account its extra layer of security, so after setup you'll sign in with your password *plus* a verification code from the app or your phone.

Have your phone and your computer side by side before you start, because you'll be scanning a QR code from one to the other.

**Setting up Microsoft Authenticator**

1. On your computer, go to sign in to Microsoft 365 and key in your **username / AmIU email address**.
2. Enter your **password** and choose **Sign in**. Because MFA hasn't been registered yet, you'll be prompted for more information rather than taken straight to your mailbox.
3. Choose **Next**. First-time users are redirected to a page asking you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app — this is the default authentication method.
4. On your phone, download **Microsoft Authenticator** from the Google Play Store or App Store. It's free, and if you're unsure where to get it, the prompt page provides a download link. If it's already installed, you can skip straight ahead.
5. Back on your computer, click **Next** — a QR code will appear on screen.
6. Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and **scan the QR code**. This is what links the app to your account so it can generate codes for you.
7. Once the scan is successful, click **Next**, then click **Next** again on the following screen.
8. Enter your **country code** and **phone number**, then click **Next**. This registers your phone as a second verification method, so you're not locked out if the app is unavailable.
9. Microsoft sends a code to your mobile phone. Type the **code** in and click **Next**.
10. Click **Next** one last time — you should see a confirmation that your account has been set up successfully.

From now on, each sign-in will ask for your password first, then a dynamically generated verification code from the Authenticator app or sent to your phone. Approve or enter it and you're in.

The screenshots below show these prompts as they appear on screen, which should help you confirm you're on the right step.

A couple of things worth knowing: keep your phone with you whenever you sign in from a new device, and don't delete the account from the Authenticator app — the recovery process for a lost or replaced phone isn't covered in our Knowledge Base, so if that happens, raise a ticket with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and "Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke).

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:
Setting up two-step verification on your Office 365 account is done through the sign-in process itself — Microsoft prompts you for the extra security details the first time it needs them. Here's how to work through it.

**Before you start**

Have your mobile phone with you, and if you can, install the free **Microsoft Authenticator** app on it beforehand. The enrolment wizard offers this app as the default method, so having it ready saves a detour mid-setup (there's also a download link inside the wizard if you skip this).

**Enrolling**

1. **Sign in to Microsoft 365** with your work or school account — that's your University email address (`campus.amref.ac.ke`) and the password you were sent individually by email when your account was created. If you're a student and need to reach your mailbox, log in to the LMS, go to **Student Services** and select **Student Email**.
2. **Choose Sign in.** Because the account has two-step verification enabled, you'll be prompted for more information rather than taken straight to your inbox — this is the enrolment prompt, not an error.
3. **Choose Next** to begin setting up the extra verification.
4. **Set up the Microsoft Authenticator app.** The default authentication method is the free Microsoft Authenticator app. If you already have it installed on your mobile device, select **Next** and follow the prompts to add this account. If you don't have it installed, use the link provided on the screen to download it first, then continue.
5. **Provide your phone number** where prompted. Two-step verification on your University account works by sending a code to your phone, so this number is what completes the login process — enter it carefully, as codes will be delivered there.
6. **Finish the sign-in** by approving the request in the Authenticator app or entering the code sent to your phone. Once you land in your mailbox, enrolment is complete, and from then on every new sign-in will ask for that second approval alongside your password.

The screenshots below show the sign-in and setup prompts you'll see, so you can match them against your screen as you go.

**A couple of things to keep in mind:** keep your phone accessible whenever you sign in, since the code or app approval is now required in addition to your password. If you change or lose the phone you registered, that specific recovery scenario isn't documented in the material I have — raise a ticket with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they'll reset the enrolment for you.

*Sources: Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — Microsoft 365 additional security verification / Microsoft Authenticator setup article (Knowledgebase category), and the Student Email access article (LMS category). Help Desk portal: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke*

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
That's a common snag after a phone swap — the sign‑in approval lives in the app on your **old** device, so the new phone has to be registered afresh. Here's how to get your account working again.

**Re-register Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. Install the **Microsoft Authenticator** app on the new phone from the **Google Play Store / App Store** before you start, so it's ready when the QR code appears.
2. Go to the sign-in page and **key in your username / AmIU email address**, then **enter your password**. This is the normal starting point — the verification step comes after your password is accepted.
3. Because this is effectively a first-time device, you'll be redirected to a page prompting you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app to secure your account. If you already installed it in step 1, simply choose **Next** (there's also a download link on that page if you skipped it).
4. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and scan the QR code** shown on screen. This is the step that links your account to the new device — the old phone's entry no longer matters once this succeeds.
5. Once the scan is successful, click **Next**, then **Next** again on the confirmation screen.
6. **Enter your country code and your phone number**, then click **Next**. This adds a backup verification route in case you lose access to the app again.
7. Microsoft sends a **code to your mobile phone** — type it in and click **Next**, then **Next** on the final screen.
8. You should see the confirmation that your account is set up. Sign in once more to verify: your new phone should now receive the approval prompt.

The screenshots below show these setup screens in sequence, so you can check you're on the right page at each stage.

**If you'd rather not use the app**

At the verification step, select **I want to set up a different method** and choose SMS. Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send you a **6-digit code** to verify the device. Do note the guidance here: an authenticator app is faster and more secure than SMS verification.

**Worth knowing:** you generally only need the additional verification the first time you sign in to a new app or device, or after a password change — so once this new phone is registered, you shouldn't be prompted daily.

**One caveat:** if you never reach the setup/QR-code page — for example, sign-in keeps demanding approval from the old phone and offers no way to add a new method — clearing that old registration isn't something the Knowledge Base documents. In that case raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can reset the registration on your account.

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this. VAS exams have two distinct parts: a one-off SMOWL registration that must be done **before** exam week, and then sitting the exam itself with SMOWL monitoring active.

## Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this first)

1. **Register at least 72 hours before your exams start.** SMOWL needs time to process the reference images it captures of you, so leaving this to the last minute can lock you out of your exam.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and sign in with your **email address and password** when prompted.
3. Click the **"My Courses"** button, then click the exam you want to register for.
4. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** item. This is what takes you through to the SMOWL registration page — the registration link lives inside the exam in the VAS portal, not on a separate site.
5. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, as that is the identity SMOWL ties your captured images to.
6. **Allow camera access** when your browser asks, so SMOWL can capture your image. This step is essential — if webcam access is blocked, SMOWL cannot capture your reference photos and your registration will not complete.

## Part 2 — Sit the exam

1. Use the **Google Chrome** browser for the best experience.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and select your exam in VAS.
3. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** paper.
4. Sit the exam as normal. SMOWL runs in the background **recording all your activities during the exam session**, so keep your webcam unobstructed and stay in view throughout.
5. When you have finished, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

The three screenshots below show these VAS screens, which should help you match what you're seeing on your own screen.

One gap worth flagging: the detailed middle steps of the exam-taking sequence (between opening the paper and submitting) aren't spelled out in the Help Desk material I have, so if you hit a specific snag at that point — a SMOWL check that won't pass, or a camera error mid-exam — raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke rather than waiting it out.

observations.question: What is SMOWL proctoring and how do I use it?

4. Once you've granted the necessary permissions, you'll be able to see the SMOWL dashboard, which will display a live feed of your surroundings. This is to ensure that you're not accessing any external resources or collaborating with others during the exam.
5. Throughout the exam, you'll be monitored by the SMOWL proctoring software, which will detect any suspicious activity or attempts to cheat. If you encounter any issues or have questions, you can reach out to the exam proctors for assistance.

**It's essential to note that SMOWL proctoring is designed to ensure the security and integrity of exams, and any attempts to cheat or compromise the exam process will be detected and reported.**

observations.question: smwol camera not workng during my exam
observations.answer:
That's a stressful thing to hit mid-exam — let's get the camera talking to SMOWL again. In almost every case this comes down to the webcam permissions not being granted (or the SMOWL software not actually being launched), so work through the following in order.

**1. Grant webcam and microphone permissions in your browser.** On the SMOWL pre-test page, your browser must be allowed to use the webcam and microphone — if these were blocked or dismissed, SMOWL has no camera feed to capture.

**2. Tick the checkbox to allow SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam.** This appears on the pre-test page after the browser permissions are enabled, and it is the step most often skipped.

**3. Select the "Open SMOWL" option.** This actually launches the monitoring software rather than just the web page.

**4. Confirm the software has launched — the SMOWL icon will display navy blue.** If the icon is not navy blue, the software has not started and no camera capture is happening yet.

**5. Only then click "Attempt quiz", followed by "Start attempt".**

**6. Verify SMOWL is recording.** The tool should be in **"activity in progress" mode and show a red "END ACTIVITY" button** — that red button is your confirmation that the camera is capturing. Remember that SMOWL monitors and records all your activity for the whole session.

**7. When you're done, click "Submit and finish" to end the exam.**

If the icon never turns navy blue or SMOWL never captured your image in the first place, your registration or installation may be incomplete. Redo it as follows:

1. Go to the SMOWL registration page and enter your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address** — the email must be your mcampus one so your captures are matched to your student record.
2. **Allow camera access** so SMOWL can capture your reference image; this capture is what your exam images are compared against, so it cannot be skipped.
3. **Download and install the SMOWL software** — check your Downloads folder and run the installer. Your device must meet the requirements: **Windows 10/11 or macOS 10.15+**, plus a stable internet connection.
4. **Complete registration**, then return to your CAT or Final Exam and repeat steps 1–6 above.

The screenshots below show the permission prompt and the SMOWL status icons so you can compare with what's on your screen.

One caveat: deeper hardware-level camera faults (for example a faulty webcam, missing drivers, or another application holding the camera) aren't covered in the Help Desk articles, so if SMOWL still can't see you after granting permissions and reinstalling, raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke — ideally before your exam window closes.

observations.question: How do I take an exam with webcam monitoring?
observations.answer:
Webcam-monitored exams at Amref run through SMOWL proctoring inside the Virtual Assessment System (VAS). There are two parts: a one-off registration that teaches SMOWL to recognise your face, and then the exam session itself.

**Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this at least 72 hours before exams start)**

1. Go to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and log in.
2. Open the **SMOWL registration link** in the portal — this takes you to the SMOWL registration page.
3. Enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address rather than a personal one, so your captured images are tied to your official student identity.
4. **Allow camera access** when your browser prompts you, so SMOWL can capture your reference images. This step is essential — without those images the system has nothing to match you against during the exam.
5. **Download and install the SMOWL software.** Check your Downloads folder and run the installer. Confirm your setup meets the requirements first: **Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+**, plus a stable internet connection.
6. Complete the registration.

Registering early matters: leaving it to the last minute gives you no room to fix a camera, install or connectivity problem before the exam window opens.

**Part 2 — Sit the exam**

1. Log in to the VAS portal and click to open your **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
2. Allow **SMOWL to open** and **accept the permissions** it requests.
3. On the pre-test page, enable **webcam and microphone permissions in your browser**, then tick the **checkbox to allow SMOWL to run** directly at the start of the exam.
4. Select **Open SMOWL** to launch the proctoring session. From this point SMOWL records your activity throughout the exam session, so stay in front of your camera and keep the software running.
5. When you have finished answering, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

The screenshots below show these screens as they appear in VAS, which should help you confirm you're in the right place at each stage.

Two caveats worth knowing: the guide doesn't spell out the intermediate on-screen prompts between launching SMOWL and submitting, and it doesn't document what to do if SMOWL fails to open or your webcam isn't detected — if either happens, raise it with the Help Desk rather than starting the exam without proctoring.

observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Your university (corporate) email is reached through the LMS, and the first login is what activates the account. Here's the full process.

**Before you start:** Amref sends each student an individual message containing their corporate/University email address and the account password. You'll need that message, because the password is only supplied that way.

1. **Confirm your email address.** The format is `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`. This is the corporate email created for you to access campus resources.
2. **Log in to the LMS** and go to **Student Services**, then select **Student Email**. This is the entry point to your mailbox from within the LMS.
3. **Enter your email address and the password** that was sent to you in the credentials message.
4. **Complete two-step verification.** The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number; a code is then sent to that number, and entering it completes the login.
5. **You're now activated.** Logging in successfully *is* the activation of the account — there's no separate activation step to perform. Once you're in, the mailbox is live and ready to use.

A couple of things worth knowing:

- If you never received (or can't find) the message with your email address and password, that's the one step you can't do on your own — raise it with the Help Desk so your credentials can be re-sent. When you submit a ticket you'll get an email confirming the request, plus a notification whenever the ticket is updated.
- Keep your phone handy each time you sign in from a new place, since the verification code is sent by text to the number you register.
- Note that resetting your **student portal** password is a separate process from your email login — let me know if that's what you were after and I'll walk you through it.

The screenshots below show the LMS screens for these steps.

**Sources:**

observations.question: Hello, how can I contact the AmIU Help Desk?
observations.answer:
Happy to help — there are three ways to reach the AmIU Help Desk, and the ticket route is the one that gets your issue tracked and answered.

**Option 1 — Through the LMS**

1. Log in to the LMS and hover over the **"Student Services"** menu in the navigation bar.
2. Click the **Help Desk** link that appears. This takes you straight to the help desk portal without needing to remember the address.

**Option 2 — Go directly to the portal**

**Option 3 — Send an email**

1. Email **helpdesk@amref.ac.ke**. A ticket is created and assigned to you automatically, so you don't have to fill in any form.

**Submitting a ticket on the portal**

1. Once the help desk has launched, click the **"Submit a Ticket"** button.
2. Select the **category** that matches the area you need assistance with — this routes your request to the right support staff.
3. On the online form that opens, enter your **name**, **email**, and **admissions/registration number** so your request can be matched to your student record.
4. Select the **priority** of the issue, enter a **subject**, and write a **clear message** describing the assistance you need — the more specific you are, the faster the team can resolve it.
5. Attach any **files** (for example, a screenshot of an error) if you have them.
6. Click **"Submit Ticket"**.

**What happens next**

Your ticket is forwarded to the university help desk staff, and you'll receive an email confirming that your request was received. Any time there's a change or update to your ticket, you'll get another email notification — so keep an eye on your inbox rather than resubmitting the same issue.

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Resetting your portal password is a self-service process — you can do the whole thing yourself from the login page, as long as you have your phone with you.

**How to reset your Student Portal password**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login page.
2. Key in your **Amref student email** and the **characters displayed** on screen. Your student email follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` — the characters shown are a verification check, so type them exactly as they appear.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you via text**. This is how the system confirms it's really you, so use the phone number registered with the university.
4. Type in your **new password**, **confirm it**, then click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** — this last step confirms the reset actually worked.

**Your new password must meet these rules**, or it will be rejected:

- **Length:** a minimum of **10 characters**.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

The screenshots below walk through the same screens if you'd like to follow along visually.

A couple of things to watch for: if the text message with the code doesn't arrive, it usually means the phone number on your record differs from the one you're entering — that needs to be corrected by the Help Desk before the reset can complete. Also note that your **student portal** password and your **student email** password are separate; this procedure resets the portal one only.

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this — setting up Microsoft Authenticator is a one-time process, and it adds a second layer of security so that your password alone isn't enough for someone to get into your account.

**Before you start:** have your phone with you, since you'll need to scan a code with it partway through and also receive an SMS.

1. **Install the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone** from the Google Play Store or the App Store. It's free. (If you skip this step, the sign-in page will offer you a download link when it asks for it.)
2. **Sign in to Microsoft 365** with your work/school account as you normally do — key in your username / AmIU email address.
3. **Enter your password.**
4. Because you're a first-time user, you'll be **prompted for more information** and redirected to a page telling you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app to secure your account. Choose **Next**.
5. The default authentication method is the free **Microsoft Authenticator app**. Select **Next** and follow the prompts to add this account — the screen will then display a **QR code**.
6. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and scan the QR code.** This is what links your account to the app, so the app can generate your verification codes from then on.
7. Once the scan succeeds, click **Next**, then click **Next** again on the confirmation screen.
8. **Enter your country code and phone number**, then click **Next**. This registers your phone as a second way to verify you, in case the app isn't available.
9. Microsoft will **send a code by SMS to your mobile phone**. **Enter the code** and click **Next**.
10. Click **Next** one last time — you'll see a confirmation that your account is set up successfully.

From this point on, whenever you sign in you'll enter your password and then type the dynamically generated verification code from the Authenticator app (or the one sent to your phone), so keep your phone within reach at sign-in time.

The screenshots below show the sign-in prompts as they appear on screen, which helps you confirm you're on the right page at each stage.

If you get stuck at a particular step — for example the QR code won't scan or the SMS code never arrives — tell me where it stops and I'll help from there; anything involving a lost or replaced phone isn't covered in the guides I have, so for that you'd need the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources:**
- "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase
- "Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
Switching phones is one of the most common reasons Authenticator suddenly locks you out — your account is still registered to the app on your old device, so the new phone has nothing to approve with. The fix is to re-register Authenticator on your new phone by walking through the setup prompt again.

**Re-registering Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. Install **Microsoft Authenticator** on your new phone first, from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Having it ready means you won't stall halfway through the sign-in prompts. (If you skip this, a download link is also offered during setup.)
2. Go to sign in and key in your **username / AmIU email address**, then enter your **password**.
3. When the security-information prompt appears, choose **Next**. The default method offered is the free Microsoft Authenticator app — select **Next** to add the account to your new device.
4. A **QR code** appears on screen. Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and **scan the QR code** — this is what binds your account to the new device in place of the old one.
5. Once the scan succeeds, click **Next**, then **Next** again to continue.
6. Enter your **country code and phone number**, then click **Next**. This adds a phone number as a backup verification route.
7. Microsoft sends a **code by SMS** to that number. Type the code in and click **Next**, then **Next** on the confirmation screen.
8. You should see the confirmation that your account is set up. Test it by signing in once more — the approval request should now arrive on your new phone.

The screenshots below show these prompts as they appear on screen, which helps confirm you're on the right step.

**If you'd rather not use the app on the new phone:** at the method-selection stage choose **I want to set up a different method**. Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send a 6-digit SMS code to verify the device. That said, the authenticator app is the faster and more secure option, so it's the recommended route.

Two things worth knowing: you generally only get asked for this extra verification the first time you sign in on a new app or device, or after a password change — so it shouldn't nag you daily once the new phone is registered.

One gap I should be upfront about: if the sign-in never offers you the setup screen and instead insists on approval from your old phone, removing that old device registration isn't something the Help Desk Knowledge Base documents. In that case, raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can reset your security information for you.

- *Microsoft 365 additional verification methods (Authenticator app / SMS)* — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Sitting a proctored exam has two distinct stages — a one-off SMOWL registration, then the exam session itself. Here's the whole path from start to submission.

**Stage 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this at least 72 hours before exams start)**

Registering early matters because SMOWL has to capture and store your reference image before it can verify you on exam day.

observations.question: What is SMOWL proctoring and how do I use it?
observations.answer:
I can sense your frustration with understanding how SMOWL proctoring works. Let's break it down step by step.

To use SMOWL proctoring, you need to understand the process of a proctored exam. Here's what happens during a proctored exam with SMOWL:

1. Before the exam, the lecturer sets up the exam in the VAS-Exam system, which includes configuring SMOWL proctoring. This involves setting up the exam settings, such as the duration and any specific rules for the exam.
2. During the exam, the student will be required to take the exam while being monitored by SMOWL. This means that the student's screen will be recorded, and their activity will be monitored in real-time.
3. The lecturer can then review the recorded exam session to ensure that the student was not cheating.

To use SMOWL proctoring, lecturers need to follow these steps:

1. Go to the VAS-Exam system and click on the "Create Exam" button.
2. Fill in the required details, such as the exam name, duration, and any specific rules for the exam.
3. Click on the "Add Question" button to add questions to the exam.
4. Once the exam is set up, the lecturer can schedule the exam and send it to the students.
5. During the exam, the student will be required to take the exam while being monitored by SMOWL.
6. After the exam, the lecturer can review the recorded exam session to ensure that the student was not cheating.

**Important:** Make sure that you have a stable internet connection and a compatible device to take the proctored exam.

You can find more information on SMOWL proctoring and how to use it in the following articles:

* How-Smowl-works.pdf
* Lecturer-Tutorial-v001.pdf
* Lecturer Exams Proctoring training

These resources will provide you with a more detailed understanding of how SMOWL proctoring works and how to use it effectively.

**Caveats:** Please note that SMOWL proctoring requires a stable internet connection and a compatible device to function properly. If you experience any issues during the exam, please contact the IT department for assistance.

observations.question: smwol camera not workng during my exam
observations.answer:
A camera failing mid‑exam is stressful — let's get SMOWL seeing you again. In almost every case the camera stalls because the browser permission wasn't granted (or was dismissed), the "allow SMOWL to run" checkbox wasn't ticked, or the SMOWL software never actually launched. Work through these in order:

**1. Grant webcam and microphone permission in your browser.**
On the SMOWL pre‑test page, your browser must have webcam *and* microphone permissions enabled. If you clicked "Block" or closed the prompt, SMOWL gets no video feed at all. Re‑enable them and reload the exam page.

**2. Tick the checkbox to allow SMOWL to run.**
After the permissions are enabled, you must click the checkbox that allows SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam — skipping this leaves the tool inactive even though your camera itself is fine.

**3. Select "Open SMOWL".**
This is the step that actually launches the monitoring software. Confirm it launched: **the SMOWL icon displays navy blue once the software has launched.** If the icon never turns navy blue, SMOWL isn't running and no images are being captured.

**4. Check you are in monitoring mode before answering questions.**
Go back into the exam via **"Attempt quiz"** then **"Start attempt"**. SMOWL should now be in **"activity in progress"** mode and show a **red "END ACTIVITY" button**. That red button is your proof the camera is recording. If the button isn't red, SMOWL is not monitoring — fix that before continuing.

**5. If SMOWL still can't see you, re‑check your registration and installation.**
Your camera also has to have been captured during SMOWL registration. On the SMOWL registration page:
- Enter your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address** — the email must be your mcampus one so the captured images link to your exam account.
- **Allow camera access** so the system can capture your image; SMOWL cannot verify you without this.
- **Download and install the SMOWL software** — open your Downloads folder and run the installer.
- Confirm your system meets the requirements: **Windows 10 or 11 / macOS 10.15+** and a **stable internet connection**. An older OS or a dropping connection will stop the camera feed.
- Complete the registration.

**6. Finish properly.** When you're done with the paper, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

Keep in mind that SMOWL monitors and records all your activity for the whole session, so stay in front of the camera once it's working.

The screenshots below show what these SMOWL screens and indicators look like. What isn't documented in our Help Desk material is device‑level camera faults (for example another application holding the camera, or hardware/driver issues) — if the steps above don't restore the feed, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke right away so your exam session can be assisted while it's still open.

Sources:
- VAS‑Exam system — SMOWL exam access and permissions (VAS-Exam system Knowledge Base)
- VAS‑Exam system — SMOWL registration and software installation (VAS-Exam system Knowledge Base)

observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Getting into your Amref email is straightforward once you know the address format and that the first login doubles as the activation step.

**How to access your university email**

1. **Find your login details in the welcome communication.** Your corporate/University email address and its initial password are sent individually to each student, so check the message you received — the password is not something you create yourself at this stage.
2. **Confirm your email address format.** Your university address is `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`. Using the wrong format (a nickname, or a middle name) is a common reason a login fails.
3. **Open the LMS and go to Student Services, then select Student Email.** This is the route into your mailbox from the learning platform, and it's where your campus resources are linked together (see the screenshots below).
4. **Log in with your email address and the password that was sent to you.** Note that **logging in is what activates the account** — until you sign in for the first time, the email isn't usable, so don't skip this even if you're not expecting mail yet.
5. **Complete the two-step verification.** The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number, and a code will be sent to it. Enter that code to finish signing in. Keep the phone you registered nearby each time you log in from a new place, since this step protects the account from someone using a leaked password.

**A couple of things worth knowing**

- Your university email is the key to other services too — for instance, resetting your Student Portal password at `https://students.amref.ac.ke/#` requires your Amref student email, so having the mailbox activated first saves you trouble later.
- If the password you were sent doesn't work, or you no longer have access to the phone number used for two-step verification, the fix isn't documented in the knowledge base — raise a ticket with the University Help Desk. Once you submit it, you'll get an email confirming the request, plus a notification whenever there's an update on it.

Sources: Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — "Student Email" (LMS category) and "Reset your student portal password" (Knowledgebase category). For anything the steps above don't resolve, you can reach the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — resetting your portal password is a self-service process you can complete in a few minutes, as long as you have your Amref student email address and your phone handy.

**Steps to reset your student portal password**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen.
2. Key in your **Amref student email** (the corporate address in the format firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke) and then type in the **characters displayed** on screen — this is the verification check that confirms a person, not a bot, is requesting the reset.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you via text**. This step confirms your identity, so the number must be the one held on your student record.
4. Type in your **new password**, confirm it in the second field, then click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** — logging in successfully is how you confirm the reset actually took effect.

**Your new password must meet these rules**, or the system will reject it:

- **Length:** a minimum of 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not be any of your official names**.

A couple of things worth knowing: the reset depends on the email address and phone number registered against your account, so if the text code never arrives or your email isn't recognised at step 2, that's a records issue rather than a password issue — the Help Desk will need to sort it out for you at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke. Also note that your portal password is separate from your student email password, so changing one doesn't change the other.

The screenshots below show the reset screens you'll be moving through, which may help you confirm you're in the right place.

Sources:
- *Reset your student portal password* (Knowledgebase)
- *Student Portal* — https://students.amref.ac.ke/

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — the whole thing takes about five minutes, and you'll need your phone next to you.

**What you're setting up:** Multi-factor authentication (MFA) on your Microsoft 365 account, so that after your password you also confirm a dynamically generated verification code from the authenticator app or sent to your phone. That second step is what stops someone signing in with a stolen password.

**Steps**

1. Go to sign in to Microsoft 365 with your work/school account and key in your **username / AmIU email address**.
2. Enter your **password** and choose **Sign in**. You'll then be prompted for more information.
3. Choose **Next**. As a first-time user you'll be redirected to a page asking you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app — this is the app that will secure your account.
4. On your phone, download **Microsoft Authenticator** from the Google Play Store or the App Store. The free Microsoft Authenticator app is the default authentication method; if you already have it installed, just select **Next** and follow the prompts to add the account, and if you don't, a download link is provided on that page.
5. Back on your computer, click **Next**.
6. Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and **scan the QR code** displayed on your screen — this links your account to the app so it can generate your codes.
7. Once the scan is successful, click **Next**.
8. Click **Next** again.
9. Enter your **country code** and your **phone number**, then click **Next**. This registers your phone so a code can also be sent to you directly.
10. You'll receive a code from Microsoft on your mobile phone. Enter the code and click **Next**.
11. Click **Next** one final time — your account is now set up.

**Worth knowing**

- Keep the app installed on the phone you used during setup; from now on, every sign-in will ask for the verification code from that app (or sent to your phone) after your password.
- If you change or lose that phone, you'll need MFA re-registered on your account before you can sign in again — raise that with the Help Desk.

The screenshots below show the setup screens as they'll appear to you, so you can match each step against what's on your display.

**Sources:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and "Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke).

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
That's a common snag after a phone swap — the account registration lived on your old device, so your new phone has nothing to approve with. Here's how to get the Authenticator working again on the new handset.

**Re-registering Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. Install **Microsoft Authenticator** on the new phone first, from the Google Play Store or the App Store, so it's ready when the sign-in flow asks for it. (If you skip this, the sign-in page also gives you a download link at the right moment.)
2. Go to sign in and key in your **username / AmIU email address**, then enter your **password**. This is what triggers the security-setup prompt.
3. When the page asking you to set up the Microsoft Authenticator app appears, choose **Next**. The Authenticator app is the default authentication method because it's the faster and more secure option.
4. A **QR code** will be displayed. Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and **scan the QR code** — this is the step that links your AmIU account to the new device.
5. Once the scan succeeds, click **Next**, then **Next** again as prompted.
6. Enter your **country code and phone number**, then click **Next**. This adds a phone verification method as a backup.
7. Microsoft will send a **code** to your mobile phone. Type the code in and click **Next**, then **Next** once more to finish. You should see the confirmation that your account is set up successfully.

The screenshots below show what these setup screens look like as you work through them.

**If you'd rather not use the app**

At the setup prompt you can select **I want to set up a different method** and choose SMS instead. Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send you a **6-digit code** to verify the device. It works, though the app is the recommended option.

**Worth knowing**

- You'll generally only be asked for this extra verification the first time you sign in on a new app or device, or after a password change — so expect the prompt now, but not daily afterwards.
- **If sign-in won't let you reach the setup screen at all** — for example it keeps demanding approval from the old phone that you no longer have — clearing that old registration isn't something the knowledge base documents. In that case log a ticket with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and ask for your MFA registration to be reset, then run through the steps above.

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this — it's a two-part process: you register once on SMOWL (the proctoring software), then sit the exam through the same VAS portal.

**Part 1 — Register on SMOWL before your exam**

1. **Register at least 72 hours before exams start.** SMOWL needs time to capture and process your reference images, so leaving this to the last minute risks being locked out of your paper.
2. Open **Google Chrome** — this browser gives the best experience with VAS and SMOWL — and go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke**.
3. Enter your **email address and password** when prompted to log in.
4. Select the **"My Courses"** button, then click the exam you want.
5. Click to open **CAT** or **Final Exams**. This is what takes you through to the SMOWL registration page (the screenshots below show these screens).
6. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, so your registration is matched to your student record.
7. **Allow camera access** when your browser asks, so SMOWL can capture your image. This step is essential — if you block the webcam, SMOWL cannot create the reference images it uses to verify you during the exam.

**Part 2 — Take the exam**

1. Again in **Google Chrome**, go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and select your exam in VAS.
2. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** paper.
3. Sit the paper as normal, keeping in mind that SMOWL is **recording all your activities throughout the exam session** — so stay in front of your webcam and keep it unobstructed.
4. When you have finished, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

One caveat: the detailed intermediate steps between opening the paper and submitting it (the on-screen prompts SMOWL shows once the exam begins) aren't fully spelled out in the material I have here. If you need those specifics, or your camera check fails during registration, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke — and do it well inside that 72-hour window.

observations.question: smwol camera not workng during my exam
observations.answer:
That's stressful to hit mid-exam — let's get your webcam recognised by SMOWL. In most cases the camera itself is fine and SMOWL simply hasn't been granted permission or hasn't fully launched, so work through these checks in order.

**1. Grant webcam and microphone permissions in your browser.** On the SMOWL pre-test page, your browser will prompt for camera and microphone access — you must accept both. If you dismissed or blocked that prompt earlier, SMOWL has nothing to record from, which is the most common cause of a "camera not working" message.

**2. Tick the checkbox that allows SMOWL to run at the start of the exam.** After the browser permissions are enabled, this checkbox on the pre-test page is what authorises the tool to launch — skipping it leaves SMOWL inactive even though your camera is fine.

**3. Select the "Open SMOWL" option.** This actually starts the monitoring software rather than just the web page.

**4. Confirm the software has launched — the SMOWL icon will display navy blue.** A navy blue icon means the application is running on your machine. If it never turns navy blue, SMOWL isn't installed or isn't starting, so continue to step 6.

**5. Verify you are being monitored.** Once you click **"Attempt quiz"** and then **"Start attempt"**, the SMOWL tool should be in **"activity in progress"** mode and display a **red button reading END ACTIVITY**. That red button is your proof the camera is capturing — if it's showing, your exam is being recorded correctly and you can proceed, finishing with **"Submit and finish"**.

**6. If the icon never goes navy blue, check your SMOWL installation.** Download and install the SMOWL software (look in your Downloads folder and run the installer), and confirm your machine meets the requirements: Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15 or later, plus a stable internet connection. An unsupported operating system or an installer that was downloaded but never run will stop the camera from being detected.

**7. Re-check your SMOWL registration.** Registration requires you to enter your full name and your Amref (mcampus) email address, then **allow camera access so SMOWL can capture your image**. If you blocked the webcam at that stage, your registration images were never captured and the exam-time camera check can fail — complete the registration again, allowing camera access this time.

The screenshots below show these SMOWL screens so you can compare them against what's on your display.

One caveat: deeper hardware-level causes — camera drivers, another application holding the webcam, or the specific menu path for resetting a blocked permission in your particular browser — aren't documented in the Help Desk articles. **If your exam is live and the red END ACTIVITY button still won't appear, contact the Help Desk immediately rather than continuing, so your attempt isn't flagged as unmonitored.** Reach them at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

Sources:
- VAS-Exam system — SMOWL exam access and permissions (Article 1)
- VAS-Exam system — SMOWL registration and software installation (Article 2)

## Stage 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this at least 72 hours before exams start)

2. **Click to open your CAT or Final Exam.**
3. On the **pre-test page**, enable **webcam and microphone permissions** in your browser when prompted — SMOWL cannot start without both.
4. Tick the **checkbox that allows SMOWL to run** at the start of the exam, then select **Open SMOWL** and accept the permissions. SMOWL now records your activities for the whole exam session, so stay in view of the camera.
5. Sit the exam as normal, and when you're finished click **"Submit and finish"** to end it.

A couple of things worth knowing: if SMOWL refuses to launch, the usual causes are browser webcam/microphone permissions that weren't accepted, or the allow-SMOWL checkbox not being ticked on the pre-test page — go back through step 3 and 4 before anything else. observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Getting into your university (corporate) email for the first time is mostly a matter of logging in through the LMS — here's the full path.

**Where your email lives and what it's called**

Your university email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`. The password is sent to you individually: each student receives a communication containing both their corporate/University email address and the account password, so check that message before you start.

**Steps to access it**

1. Log in to the **LMS**, since the email is reached through it rather than a separate address you have to remember.
2. On the LMS, go to **Student Services** and select **Student Email**. The screenshots below show where this sits.
3. Enter your email address in the `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` format, then the password you were sent.
4. Complete **two-step verification**. The account has this enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number, and a code will be sent to it by text — enter that code to finish signing in.
5. You're in. Note that this first successful login is what **activates** the account — logging in *is* the activation, so there's no separate activation step to hunt for.

**Worth knowing**

- Until you log in once, the account is not yet activated, which is why some campus resources may not accept it beforehand.
- Your phone must be reachable for the verification text, as you can't complete the login without that code.
- If the message with your credentials never arrived, or the verification code doesn't come through, raise a ticket with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke — you'll get an email confirming the request, plus a notification whenever the ticket is updated.

One clarification, in case it's what you're actually after: the password sent to you is for your **email account**. Resetting a forgotten **student portal** password is a separate process at https://students.amref.ac.ke/# via "forgot your password" — just say the word if that's the one you need.

observations.question: I cannot log in to my Amref systems. Can you help me?
observations.answer:
I'm sorry you're locked out — that's stressful, especially around deadlines. Since "Amref systems" all hang off your Amref account, let's work through the three login paths in the order that fixes most cases: your Amref email (which everything else depends on), then the LMS, then the Student Portal.

## 1. Start with your Amref student email — it's the key to the rest

Your LMS sign-in goes through your Amref email account, so if the email account isn't working, nothing else will either.

1. Your email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** — for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke. The password was sent to you: the details to access this account are sent individually to each student, in a message containing your corporate/University email address and its password.
2. Log in with those details. The account has to be **ACTIVATED before you can use it, and logging in is what activates it** — so a brand-new account that has never been signed into is a very common reason a first login attempt fails elsewhere.
3. Have your phone next to you. The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked to enter your phone number, and a code will be sent to it that you must input to complete the login. Without that code the login won't finish.
4. Once the account works, you can reach it any time from the LMS: under **Student Services**, select **Student Email**.

## 2. Logging in to the LMS (lms.amref.ac.ke)

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. At the top right of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
3. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — this is the step people miss; the LMS has no separate password of its own, it authenticates you through your Amref email account.
4. You'll be redirected to the AMREF email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password, and you'll be taken to your dashboard.
5. On the left navigation of the dashboard, go to **My courses** and pick the course you want to study (for example, "Induction module").

If step 4 rejects your credentials, the fault is with the email account itself — go back to section 1.

## 3. Student Portal — reset the password if it's forgotten

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"**.
2. Key in your Amref student email and the characters displayed on screen.
3. Key in your phone number, then the code sent to you via text — so the number you enter must be the one that can receive the SMS.
4. Type in your new password, confirm it, and click **Finish**. Then go back to the portal and log in with your student email and the new password.

Your new password must be at least **10 characters** long, combine uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters, and must not be any of your official names — resets are commonly refused for falling short on one of these.

The screenshots below show these login and password-reset screens so you can match what you're seeing.

**A couple of things that aren't documented here:** if you never received the message containing your email address and password, or the SMS verification code never arrives (for instance because the phone number on record is out of date), that recovery route isn't covered in the guides — raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so staff can verify your details.

If you tell me which system you're stuck on and the exact message you're seeing, I can narrow this down further.

**Sources:** "How to login to LMS" (LMS category) · "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category) · "Reset your student portal password" (Knowledgebase category) — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — resetting the portal password is a self-service process you can complete in a few minutes, as long as you have your Amref student email and your registered phone handy.

**Resetting your Student Portal password**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen.
2. Enter your **Amref student email address** (this is your corporate/University email in the format *firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke*) along with the **characters displayed** on screen — that character check is just there to confirm you're a real person and not an automated request.
3. Enter your **phone number**, then key in the **code sent to you by text**. This is how the portal verifies the request is genuinely yours, so the number must be the one registered on your student record.
4. Type your **new password**, **confirm it**, and click **Finish**.
5. Return to the portal and log in with your **student email and the new password** to confirm the reset worked.

**Password requirements** — the portal will reject a password that doesn't meet these:

- **Length:** at least 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not be any of your official names**.

A couple of things to watch for: if the SMS code doesn't arrive, it's usually because the phone number you entered doesn't match the one held on your student record, so double-check the number before requesting again. And note that this reset applies to the Student Portal — if it's actually your student email password you're stuck on, those credentials are sent to you individually by email and that account also has two-step verification enabled, where a code goes to your phone to complete login.

The screenshots below show these steps as they appear on screen.

**Sources:**

- *Student Portal* (Student Portal category), including the Student-Portal-User-Guide-ED.pdf — https://students.amref.ac.ke/

If the reset still fails after following these steps, the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke can check your registered details for you.

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Setting up Microsoft Authenticator is a one-time process that adds a second layer of security to your Amref account — after your password, you'll confirm each sign-in with a code from the app on your phone. Here's the full walkthrough.

**Before you start:** have your mobile phone with you, and be ready to install an app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.

1. **Go to sign in as you normally would** and key in your username / AmIU email address.
2. **Enter your password** and choose **Sign in**. Because MFA is enabled on your account, you'll be prompted for more information rather than taken straight in.
3. **Choose Next.** For first-time users, this takes you to a page asking you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app — this is the app that will secure your account.
4. **Install Microsoft Authenticator on your phone** from the Google Play Store or App Store. If you already have it installed, you can move straight on; if not, the sign-in page also provides a download link.
5. **Click Next** on the computer screen once the app is installed. A **QR code** will be displayed.
6. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and scan the QR code** shown on your screen. This is what links the app to your Amref account, so the codes it generates are recognised as yours.
7. **Once the scan is successful, click Next**, then **Next** again to continue.
8. **Enter your country code and your phone number**, then click **Next**. This sets up a backup verification method in case you lose access to the app.
9. **Check your phone for the code sent by Microsoft**, type it into the field, and click **Next**.
10. **Click Next** on the confirmation screen. You should now see a success message — your account is set up, and from here on you'll approve sign-ins or enter a generated code from the app after your password.

The screenshots below show what these screens look like as you move through them.

A couple of things worth knowing: keep the phone you enrolled, since every future sign-in will need it, and make sure you complete the phone-number step rather than skipping it — that number is your fallback if your phone is ever unavailable. If the QR code doesn't scan or you get stuck partway through, the Help Desk can reset your MFA registration so you can start again.

**Sources:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and "Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke).

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
Changing phones does trip this up for almost everyone — the registration lives on the old handset, so your new phone starts out with nothing to approve with. Here's how to re-register Authenticator on the new device.

**Re-register Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. **First, install the app on the new phone** — download **Microsoft Authenticator** from the Google Play Store or the App Store. Do this before you start the sign-in, because the setup screens will ask you to scan a code with it.
2. **On a computer, go to sign in** and key in your **username / AmIU email address**, then enter your **password**.
3. **At the additional-security prompt, choose Next.** The default authentication method is the free Microsoft Authenticator app; since you've just installed it, select **Next** and follow the prompts to add the account.
4. **Scan the QR code.** Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and scan the QR code displayed on screen — this is the step that ties your account to the new device. Once it succeeds, click **Next**, then **Next** again.
5. **Add your phone number as backup.** Enter your **country code** and **phone number**, then click **Next**. Microsoft sends a code to that mobile number.
6. **Enter the code you received** and click **Next**, then **Next**. You should land on a confirmation that your account is set up successfully.

The screenshots below show what these setup screens look like as you work through them.

**If you'd rather not use the app:** at the method prompt, select **I want to set up a different method**. Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send you an SMS containing a 6-digit code to verify the device. The Knowledgebase does recommend the authenticator app over SMS, as it's faster and more secure.

Once you're through, you generally won't be asked for the verification code day to day — only the first time you sign into a new app or device, or after you change your password (unless the university requires it more often).

One honest caveat: if the sign-in dead-ends by insisting on approval from your **old** phone and never offers you the option to add a new method, that reset has to be done on the account side and isn't documented in the Knowledgebase. In that case, raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can clear the old device registration for you.

**Source:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and the Microsoft 365 additional-verification article, Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke).

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this. VAS exams have two distinct stages — a one-off SMOWL registration that captures your identity, and then sitting the exam itself under SMOWL screen monitoring. Here's the whole flow.

## Before you start

- **Register on SMOWL at least 72 hours before your exams begin** — leaving it to the last minute is the most common reason students get stuck on exam day.
- Use **Google Chrome** for the best experience, since SMOWL relies on browser access to your webcam.
- Have your Amref (mcampus) email address to hand — SMOWL ties your registration to that address, so a personal email won't match your exam record.

## Part 1 — Registering on SMOWL

1. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and enter your email address and password when prompted. This is the Virtual Assessment System portal, and the SMOWL registration link lives inside it.
2. Click the **"My courses"** button, then click your preferred exam.
3. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** item. Doing this is what takes you through to the SMOWL registration page — there's no separate SMOWL website to visit.
4. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**.
5. **Allow camera access** when your browser asks, so SMOWL can capture your image. This step is essential — the captured images are what SMOWL later uses to confirm it's really you sitting the exam.

## Part 2 — Sitting the exam

1. Log back in at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** in Google Chrome.
2. Select your exam in VAS.
3. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** paper.
4. Work through the exam as normal, keeping in mind that SMOWL is recording all your activities throughout the exam session.
5. When you're done, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam. Don't simply close the tab — the submission is what records your attempt.

The screenshots below show these VAS screens, which will help you confirm you're on the right page at each stage.

One thing I should flag honestly: the middle steps of the exam-sitting sequence (between opening the paper and submitting) aren't fully spelled out in the material I have, so if SMOWL stops you at a particular check or prompt during the exam, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke rather than guessing — and do so before exam day if you can.

**Sources:**
- *How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* — VAS-Exam system, Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base
- *Taking Examination With SMOWL (Screen Monitoring)* — VAS-Exam system, Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base

I can sense your frustration with the exam process, and I'm here to help you navigate it smoothly.

To take an exam with webcam monitoring using SMOWL proctoring software, follow these steps:

1. First, access the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) portal at https://vas.amref.ac.ke to register for the exam. 
2. Click on the SMOWL registration link to register on the SMOWL platform at least 72 hours before the exam starts.
3. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details - Full Name and your Amref (mcampus) email address.
4. Allow camera access to capture your image. This is crucial for the SMOWL system to capture images of you during the exam.
5. Ensure your system meets the requirements: you should be using Windows 10 or 11, or MacOS 10.15+, and have a stable internet connection.
6. Download and install the SMOWL software from the downloads file.
7. After installing the SMOWL software, complete your registration.
8. On the day of the exam, click to open CAT or Final Exams in the VAS-Exam system.
9. Allow SMOWL to open, and accept the permissions when prompted.
10. When accessing the pre-test page, enable webcam and microphone permissions in your browser, and then click the checkbox to allow SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam.
11. Select the Open SMOWL option.
12. During the exam, make sure to allow SMOWL to run in the background and monitor your activities.
13. Finally, click "submit and finish" to end the exam.

Please note that you should have a stable internet connection and a compatible operating system to ensure a smooth exam experience.

**Important:** Ensure you have allowed SMOWL to access your webcam and microphone to capture images and audio during the exam.

observations.question: How do I take an exam with webcam monitoring?
observations.answer:
Exams at Amref are monitored through SMOWL, which uses your webcam to record your activity during the session. There are two parts to this: a one-time registration on the SMOWL platform, and then the permissions you grant when you actually open the exam.

**Part 1 — Register on SMOWL before exam day**

1. Go to the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and open the SMOWL registration link there. **Do this at least 72 hours before exams start** — registration includes capturing your reference image, and if it isn't complete in time the system won't be able to verify you when the exam opens.
2. Follow the link through to the SMOWL registration page.
3. Enter your details — your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, because that's the account SMOWL ties your identity and exam records to.
4. **Allow camera access** when your browser prompts you, so SMOWL can capture your image. This captured photo is the baseline it compares against during the exam, so this step can't be skipped.
5. **Download and install the SMOWL software.** Check your Downloads folder for the file and run the installer. First confirm your machine meets the requirements: **Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+**, plus a stable internet connection.
6. Complete the registration to finish setting up.

**Part 2 — Sitting the exam**

1. Log in to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke**.
2. Click to open your **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
3. Allow SMOWL to open and **accept the permissions**. On the pre-test page, first enable **webcam and microphone permissions in your browser**, then tick the checkbox that allows SMOWL to run at the start of the exam, and finally select **Open SMOWL**. If you dismiss or block the browser prompt, SMOWL can't launch and the exam won't start properly.
4. Sit the exam as normal — SMOWL records all of your activity throughout the session.
5. When you're done, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

The screenshots below show these VAS and SMOWL screens, which should help you match what's on your own display.

One thing to flag: the documented material walks through registration and the permissions/launch steps, but it doesn't spell out the intermediate on-screen checks between launching SMOWL and submitting. If something stalls at that stage, or SMOWL refuses to launch even after granting permissions, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke — and do that well ahead of your exam window rather than during it.

Source: *VAS-Exam system — How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, VAS-Exam system category), https://vas.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this — your university (corporate) email is reached through the LMS, and there's one activation detail that catches most people out.

## Accessing your Amref university email

1. **Find your login details in the welcome communication sent to you.** Your corporate/University email address and its password are sent individually to each student, so check that message before anything else — the password is not something you set yourself at the start.
2. **Confirm your email address format.** It follows the pattern `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`. Using the wrong format is a common reason a first login fails.
3. **Log in to the LMS**, then go to **Student Services** and select **Student Email**. This is the entry point to your mailbox, so you don't need to hunt for a separate address (the screenshots below show what this looks like on the LMS).
4. **Sign in with your email address and the password you were sent.** Note that **logging in IS the activation** — your email account has to be activated before you can use it, and that activation happens simply by completing this first successful login.
5. **Complete two-step verification.** The account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number; a code is then sent to that number, and entering it finishes the login process. Keep your phone within reach before you start this step.
6. **You're in** once the mailbox loads — from there your email works for accessing campus resources.

## If you get stuck

- No welcome communication with your credentials, or the details don't work? That's the point to raise it with the Help Desk rather than retrying repeatedly.
- Worth knowing for later: your **student portal** password is separate from this. If you ever need to reset that one, go to https://students.amref.ac.ke/# and click **forgot your password**, enter your Amref student email and the displayed characters, then your phone number and the code sent by text, then set and confirm a new password. Portal passwords need at least 10 characters, a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers and special characters, and must not be any of your official names.
- When you submit a ticket, attach any relevant files and click **Submit Ticket**. It goes to the university help desk staff and you'll get an email confirming the request, plus a notification each time the ticket is updated.

**Sources:** "LMS — Student Email / Mcampus Email / Corporate Email" and "Reset your student portal password" (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base). To log a ticket: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke
