   c. Input your phone number, and a code will be sent to you via text. Enter the code, and you will be logged in to your university email.

Note that your university email account has two-step verification enabled, so you will need to input your phone number and code to complete the login process.

Also, please be aware that your university email password should meet certain requirements, including a minimum length of 10 characters, a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and should not be any of your official names.

If you encounter any issues with accessing your university email or have any other questions, feel free to ask.

**Caveat:** If you have forgotten your university email password, you can reset it by going to the student portal on https://students.amref.ac.ke/ and following the instructions to reset your password.

observations.question: Where do I sign in to my corporate Outlook account?
observations.answer:
Your Amref corporate (Outlook) mailbox is reached through the LMS, so the sign-in route runs via **lms.amref.ac.ke**. Here's the full path from a browser to your inbox.

**Step 1 — Open the LMS**
Type `lms.amref.ac.ke` into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".

**Step 2 — Sign in to the LMS**
1. At the top right of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
2. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — this hands you over to Microsoft rather than asking for a separate LMS password.
3. You'll be redirected to the Amref email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password, and you'll land on your dashboard.

**Step 3 — Open your mailbox**
On the LMS, go to **Student Services** and select **Student Email**. That's the documented entry point to your corporate mailbox.

**Your credentials**
- Your email address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`.
- The password was sent to you individually by email; that message contains both your corporate/University address and its password.
- Your first successful login *is* the activation of the account, so if you've never signed in before, this step activates the mailbox.

**Expect a two-step verification prompt**
The email account has two-step verification enabled. After you sign in to Microsoft 365 with your password as normal, you'll be prompted for more information — choose **Next**, then supply the phone number where the verification code should be sent, and enter that code to complete the login. Verification codes come either from an authenticator app or as a message to your phone.

One caveat: the knowledge base documents the LMS **Student Services → Student Email** route rather than a direct Outlook web address, so use that path. If you never received the email containing your address and password, that credential lookup isn't something the guides cover — the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke can resend those details.

The screenshots below are from the LMS and should help you recognise the login screens as you go.

**Sources**

- "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category)
- Microsoft 365 two-step verification sign-in article (Knowledgebase category)

observations.question: Hi, I forgot my password and I am locked out. Please help.
observations.answer:
Being locked out is stressful — let's get you back in. Here's how to reset your **student portal** password yourself, without waiting on anyone.

**Before you start:** you'll need your Amref student email address and access to the phone number registered on your student record, because the reset code arrives by text.

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **Forgot your password?** on the login screen.
2. Enter your **Amref student email** and type in the **characters displayed** (the captcha) — this confirms the request is coming from a person, not an automated script.
3. Enter your **phone number**, then key in the **code sent to you via text**. This is how the system verifies you own the account.
4. Type your **new password**, **confirm** it, and click **Finish**.
5. Return to the portal and log in with your **student email and new password** to confirm the reset worked.

Your new password must meet these rules, or the portal will reject it:

- **Length:** at least 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** contain any of your official names.

One thing to expect afterwards: because you've just changed your password, the next time you sign in to a university app or device you'll likely be asked for an **additional verification code** — either from the Microsoft Authenticator app or sent to you by text. That's normal after a password change, not a sign that something went wrong. Once you're through, you generally won't be prompted for it every day.

The screenshots below show the screens you'll be working through.

A couple of caveats: if the text code never arrives, the phone number on your record may be out of date, and if the password you're locked out of is your **university email / Microsoft account** rather than the student portal, that particular reset isn't documented in what I have here. In either case, raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they'll unlock it for you.

**Sources:**
- Reset your student portal password — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke)
- Setting up Microsoft Authenticator — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke)

observations.question: Hello, how can I contact the AmIU Help Desk?
observations.answer:
Happy to help — there are three ways to reach the AmIU Help Desk, and you can pick whichever is most convenient.

**Option 1 — From within the LMS**

1. Log in to the LMS and hover over the **"Student Services"** menu.
2. Click the **Help Desk** link (see the screenshot below for where this sits in the menu). This takes you straight to the help desk without needing to remember the web address.

**Option 2 — Go directly to the help desk site**

1. Visit **http://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke** in your browser. The AmIU help desk will launch as shown in the screenshots below.
2. Click the **"Submit a Ticket"** button.
3. Select the **category** that matches the area you need assistance with — choosing the right category helps route your request to the right staff.
4. On the online form that opens, enter your **name**, **email**, and **admissions/registration number**, select the **priority** of the issue, enter the **subject**, and write a clear **message** describing the assistance you need. The clearer the description, the fewer follow-up questions you'll get.
5. Attach any relevant **files** (screenshots of errors are especially useful), then click **"Submit Ticket"**.

**Option 3 — Send an email**

Email **helpdesk@amref.ac.ke** and a ticket will be created and assigned to you automatically — useful if you can't get into the LMS or the portal at all.

**What happens next**

Your ticket goes to the university help desk staff, and you'll receive an email confirming that your request was received. Every time a change is made to your ticket, you'll get an email notification, so keep an eye on the inbox of the address you submitted.

---

Source: *How to access the AmIU help desk* — Knowledgebase, http://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

**Logging in**

2. **Click 'Login/Register'** at the top right of the homepage — this is the entry point to the sign-in flow.

Your address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your university email details.
5. **Complete the two-step verification.** The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for a phone number where a code is sent — enter that code to finish signing in.
6. **Confirm you've landed on the dashboard**, then on the left navigation panel go to **"My courses"** and select the course you want to study — for example, "Induction Module". If your course opens, your login worked.

The screenshots below show the login page and dashboard so you can check each screen matches what you're seeing.

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Resetting your portal password is a self-service process — you just need access to your Amref student email and your registered phone number, since the reset code is sent by text.

**How to reset it:**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen.
2. Enter your **Amref student email address** (the format is firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke) along with the **characters displayed** in the image on screen — this is the verification step that confirms you're a real user, so type them exactly as shown.
3. Enter your **phone number**, then key in the **code sent to you via text**. This must be the number the university has on record for you, as that's where the code is delivered.
4. Type in your **new password**, **confirm it**, then click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and log in with your **student email and new password** to confirm the reset worked.

**Your new password must meet these rules, or it will be rejected:**

- **Length:** at least 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

The screenshots below walk through the same steps visually if you'd like to follow along.

A couple of things worth knowing: if the text code never arrives, that usually points to the phone number on your record being out of date, and if your student email itself isn't working (remember it needs to be activated by logging in at least once), you won't be able to complete step 2. In either of those cases, raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can verify your details.

- "Student Portal" — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base (https://students.amref.ac.ke/)

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — this is a one-time setup and takes just a few minutes. Have your phone next to you before you start.

**Setting up Microsoft Authenticator for your AmIU account**

1. **Start signing in as normal.** Key in your username / AmIU email address on the Microsoft 365 sign-in page.
2. **Enter your password** and choose **Sign in**. Because MFA is enabled, you'll be prompted for "more information" instead of going straight through — for first-time users this redirects you to a page asking you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app, which is what secures your account.
3. **Install the app on your phone** from the Google Play Store or the App Store. If you don't already have it, the sign-in page provides a download link. The Microsoft Authenticator app is the default authentication method.
4. **Click Next** on the computer screen to move to the QR code page.
5. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and scan the QR code** displayed on your screen. This is what links the app to your AmIU account, so the app can generate verification codes for you.
6. **Once the scan is successful, click Next**, then **click Next** again on the following screen.
7. **Enter your country code and phone number, then click Next.** This adds your phone as a second, backup verification method in case you don't have the app to hand.
8. **You'll receive a code from Microsoft on your mobile phone.** Type that code in and click **Next**.
9. **Click Next** on the final screen — you'll see a confirmation that your account is set up successfully.

From then on, each sign-in works the same way: you enter your password, then approve the prompt or type the dynamically generated code from the Authenticator app (or the code sent to your phone).

A couple of things worth knowing:
- The QR code page and the phone-number page look like the screenshots below, which should help you confirm you're on the right step.
- **Keep the app installed and your registered phone number current** — if you change or lose your phone, you'll need Help Desk assistance to re-register, since the app on the old device is your key to signing in.

Sources: *Setting up Microsoft Authenticator* and *Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication* (Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase). If you get stuck at any step, you can reach the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: smwol camera not workng during my exam
observations.answer:
That's a stressful thing to hit mid-exam — let's get the camera feed live again. In almost every case, SMOWL's camera fails because a permission wasn't granted, the checkbox to launch SMOWL was skipped, or the SMOWL software isn't properly installed. Work through these in order:

**1. Grant webcam and microphone permissions in your browser.**
On the pre-test page, your browser will prompt for camera and microphone access — accept both. SMOWL cannot capture anything if the browser itself is blocking the webcam, so this is the first thing to confirm.

**2. Tick the SMOWL checkbox, then select "Open SMOWL".**
After enabling the browser permissions, you must click the checkbox that allows SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam, then choose the **Open SMOWL** option. If this checkbox is missed, the tool never actually starts and the camera will appear to be doing nothing.

**3. Confirm the software has launched.**
When SMOWL launches correctly, the icon displays **navy blue**. If you never see the navy blue icon, the application isn't running on your machine.

**4. Check that the SMOWL software is installed and your system is supported.**
The SMOWL software must be downloaded and installed on your device — look in your Downloads folder and run the installer if you haven't already. Your setup needs to meet the requirements:
- Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+
- A stable internet connection

An unsupported or outdated system, or a dropped connection, will stop the camera from streaming.

**5. Verify your SMOWL registration captured your image.**
Registration is what gives SMOWL your reference photo. It requires your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**, then allowing camera access so the system can capture your image, and finally completing registration. If camera access was denied at that stage, go back through registration and allow it this time.

**6. Re-enter the exam and confirm monitoring is active.**
Open your CAT or Final Exam, click **"attempt quiz"**, then **"start attempt"**. SMOWL should now be in **"activity in progress"** mode, showing a red **END ACTIVITY** button. That red button is your proof the camera is capturing — if you can see it, you're being monitored correctly and can sit the paper.

**7. When you're done, click "submit and finish"** to end the exam.

**Remember that SMOWL monitors and records all your activity during the session — don't close it or revoke camera access part-way through your paper.**

The screenshots below show the permission prompt and the SMOWL status indicators so you can compare them against what's on your screen.

One honest limitation: if you've done all of the above and the camera still won't come on, hardware-level causes (faulty webcam, drivers, another app holding the camera) aren't covered in the Help Desk documentation. In that case, contact the Help Desk straight away at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so your exam attempt can be looked at.

**Sources:** VAS-Exam system — SMOWL registration and installation guide; VAS-Exam system — sitting your CAT/Final Exam with SMOWL permissions. Help Desk: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I access my university email?

observations.question: I cannot log in to my Amref systems. Can you help me?
observations.answer:
Sorry you're locked out — that's stressful, especially if there's coursework waiting. Since your Amref email credentials are what unlock both the LMS and the Student Portal, let's start there and then cover each system's login.

## 1. Make sure your Amref (corporate/University) email is activated

Everything else signs in with these details, so this comes first.

1. Your email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke).
2. The password was sent to you individually — the communication you received contains both your University email address and your account password.
3. **The email must be activated before you can use it, and logging in is what activates it.** If you've never signed in, that's often the reason other systems reject you.
4. The account has two-step verification enabled, so during login you'll be asked for a phone number and a code will be sent to it to complete the process — have your phone with you.
5. To reach the mailbox, open the LMS, go to **Student Services**, and select **Student Email**.

## 2. Log in to the LMS (Moodle)

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. At the top right of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
3. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — the LMS doesn't hold a separate password, it hands you over to your email account.
4. You'll be redirected to the AMREF email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password, and you'll be taken to your dashboard.
5. On the left navigation of the dashboard, go to **My courses** and pick the course you want to study (for example, "Induction module") — seeing your courses listed confirms the login worked.

## 3. Log in to the Student Portal (or reset its password)

1. Go to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**
2. If you've forgotten your password, click **forgot your password**.
3. Enter your Amref student email and the characters displayed on screen.
4. Enter your phone number, then the code sent to you via text — this is how the portal confirms it's really you.
5. Type your new password, confirm it, and click **finish**.
6. Return to the portal and log in with your student email and the new password.

Your new password must be at least **10 characters** long, mix uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters, and must not contain any of your official names — the reset will keep failing until it meets all three conditions.

Some of the screens described above are shown in the screenshots below.

**A couple of things to watch for:** if you never received the email with your account password, or the verification code by text or email never arrives, that has to be sorted out by the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke — those details are issued individually and can't be self-recovered.

If you let me know which system is refusing you (LMS, Student Portal, or your email) and the exact message you're seeing, I can narrow this down further.

Sources: "How to login to LMS" (LMS category), "Reset your student portal password" (Knowledgebase), and "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category) — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: Hi, I forgot my password and I am locked out. Please help.
observations.answer:
Being locked out is stressful — let's get you back in. Here's the full self-service password reset for the **Student Portal**, which you can complete yourself in a couple of minutes.

**Resetting your Student Portal password**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen.
2. Key in your **Amref student email address** and the **characters displayed** on screen — that character check simply confirms a person, not a bot, is making the request.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you by text**. This is the identity check, so use the number the University has on record for you; if no text arrives, the number on your record is likely different from the one you're entering.
4. Type your **new password**, **confirm** it, then click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** to verify the reset actually took effect.

**Your new password must meet these rules**, or the form will not accept it:

- **Length:** at least 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers and special characters.
- It must **not be any of your official names**.

**One thing to expect afterwards:** because you've just changed your password, the next time you sign in to an app or device you may be asked for an extra verification code — either from the **Microsoft Authenticator app** or **sent by text message**. That's normal and not a second lockout. You generally only get asked when signing into a new app or device, or right after a password change, so it shouldn't happen daily.

If that prompt appears and you've never set up Authenticator before, sign in with your **username/AmIU email address**, enter your **password**, and you'll be redirected to a page asking you to **download the Microsoft Authenticator app** — install it on your phone from the **Google Play Store or App Store** and continue from there to secure your account. The screenshots below show these screens.

Two caveats: if your lockout is on a **different account** (for example your university email or the LMS/Moodle) rather than the Student Portal, or if the **phone number on your record is out of date** so the text code never arrives, that isn't something the documented reset covers — the Help Desk will need to verify you and reset it manually at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources:** Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — "Reset your student portal password" and "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" (Knowledgebase category); Help Desk: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I use Microsoft Teams for my classes?

   - If you don't have it installed, use the download link shown on that screen to get it first.
   - From then on, you'll approve sign-ins with a code provided by the authenticator app or sent to your phone — this is what protects your university account if your password is ever guessed.

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
I can imagine how frustrating it can be to forget your password and not be able to access the student portal.

To reset your student portal password, follow these steps:

1. Go to the student portal on https://students.amref.ac.ke/ and click on "Forgot your password" if you've forgotten it.
2. Key in your Amref student email and the characters displayed in the security image.
3. Key in your phone number, and a code will be sent to you via text. Enter this code.
4. Type in your new password and confirm it, making sure it meets the password requirements: a minimum of 10 characters, a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and not any of your official names.
5. Finish the password reset process and go back to the portal to log in with your student email and new password.

Please note that your password will be sent to your email address, so make sure you have access to that email to reset your password. Also, keep in mind that your student email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll need to input your phone number to complete the login process.

**Important:** Make sure to use a strong and unique password that meets the requirements mentioned above to ensure your account's security.

Sources:

* https://students.amref.ac.ke/ (Student Portal)
* https://students.amref.ac.ke/# (Student Portal - Forgot Password)

observations.question: My Student Portal login is not working. What should I do?
observations.answer:

To reset your Student Portal password, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Student Portal on https://students.amref.ac.ke/# and click on "Forgot your password" if you've forgotten it.
2. Key in your Amref student email and the characters displayed in the Captcha field.
3. Key in your phone number, and a code will be sent to you via text. Enter this code.
4. Type in your new password and confirm it, then finish the password reset process.
5. Go back to the Student Portal and log in with your student email and new password.

It's also a good idea to ensure your new password meets the following criteria:

- It should contain a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

Please note that if you're experiencing issues with your Student Portal login, it's possible that your Amref student email may not be activated. To activate your email, follow the instructions in the LMS under Student Services, select Student Email. You will need to access the email account that has been created for you, which is in the format of firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke, and the password will be sent to you via email.

If you're still having trouble, feel free to ask, and I'll be happy to help.

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
I can sense your frustration with setting up Microsoft Authenticator, but let's break it down step by step.

To set up Microsoft Authenticator, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Microsoft Authenticator setup page (though the exact URL isn't specified in the context, it's implied to be a page where you can initiate the setup process). Key in your Amref University email address and enter your password.
2. For first-time users, you might be redirected to a page that requires you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app from the Google Store or App Store on your phone.
3. Download and install the app on your phone, then open it and click on "Next" to proceed.
4. You will be prompted to scan a QR code using your phone's camera. Open the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone and scan the QR code to link your account.
5. Once the QR code is scanned successfully, click on "Next" to continue.
6. Enter your country code and phone number, then click on "Next" to receive a verification code from Microsoft.
7. You will receive a code from Microsoft on your mobile phone. Enter the code and click on "Next" to complete the setup process.
8. Finally, click on "Next" to complete the setup process and successfully set up your account.

**Note:** Make sure you have a stable internet connection and that your phone is compatible with the Microsoft Authenticator app.

Sources:

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
I can sense your frustration with the VAS exam process. Let's walk through the steps to register and take a VAS exam with SMOWL proctoring software.

To register and take a VAS exam, follow these steps:

1. Access the SMOWL registration link in the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) portal by visiting https://vas.amref.ac.ke. This will take you to the registration page.
2. In VAS, select the "my courses" button and click on the preferred exam to proceed to the SMOWL registration page.
3. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details - Full Name and your Amref (m-campus) email address.
4. Allow camera access to capture your image by giving the SMOWL system permission to access your webcam.
5. Once you've completed the registration process, select your exam in VAS and click to open CAT or Final Exams.
6. Use Google Chrome browser for the best experience during the exam session.
7. During the exam, make sure to record all your activities and follow the instructions provided by the SMOWL system.
8. When you're finished with the exam, click "submit and finish" to end the exam.

Please note that it's essential to register at least 72 hours before the exams start to ensure a smooth registration process.

**Important:** Ensure you have the necessary permissions and meet the system requirements for the SMOWL software to function correctly.

Sources:

- Article 1: VAS-Exam system, "How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software"
- Article 2: VAS-Exam system, "Taking examination With the SMOWL (Screen Monitoring)"

observations.question: How do I log in to the LMS?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — logging into the LMS takes just a few steps once your Amref email is active.

**Before you start:** the LMS signs you in with your Amref (corporate/university) email account, so that account must already be activated. Your email address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your account details. Simply logging in for the first time is what activates the account.

**Logging in:**

1. Open your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini) and type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into the address bar — or search Google for "lms amref" if you'd rather not type the address.
2. On the homepage, click **'Login/Register'** at the top right.
3. In the pop-up window that appears, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — this is what links your LMS access to your university account rather than a separate LMS password.
4. You'll be redirected to the Amref email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password there.
5. Complete the two-step verification prompt. The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number and a code will be sent to it — enter that code to finish signing in.
6. Once verified, you'll land on your LMS dashboard. On the left navigation menu, go to **"My courses"** and select the course you want to study (for example, "Induction Module").

The screenshots below show what the login page and dashboard look like at these steps, so you can check you're on the right screen.

**A couple of things to watch for:** if you've never logged into your Amref email before, that first sign-in is your activation — there's no separate activation step to hunt for. And keep your phone nearby, since you can't get past the verification code prompt without it. You can also reach your Student Email directly from the LMS under **Student Services → Student Email**.

Happy learning!

*Source: "How to login to LMS" and "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, LMS category. If you get stuck at any step, the Help Desk is at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.*

observations.question: How do I log into Moodle?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — Moodle is the platform behind Amref's LMS, and you sign in with your Amref email account rather than a separate Moodle password.

**Logging in**

1. Open your browser (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini) and type **lms.amref.ac.ke** in the address bar — or search Google for "lms amref" if you'd rather not type the address.
2. On the LMS homepage, click **'Login/Register'** at the top right.
3. In the pop-up window that appears, click the **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** button. This hands the login over to Amref's email system, which is what actually verifies you.
4. You'll be redirected to the AMREF email login page. Enter your **Amref email address and password**, and you'll be taken straight to your LMS dashboard.
5. Once on the dashboard, look at the left navigation panel and go to **"My courses"**, then click the course you want to study — for example, "Induction Module".

The screenshots below show these login screens so you can match what's on your own display.

**If step 4 is where you get stuck**

Your LMS access depends entirely on your Amref email working, so check these:

- Your email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke), and the password was sent to you individually in a communication containing both your university email address and your account password.
- The email account must be **activated** before it will work — and activation simply means logging into it once. If you've never signed into your Amref email, do that first, then come back to the LMS.
- The email account has **two-step verification enabled**, so you'll be asked for a phone number where a code is sent to complete the login. Have your phone to hand.

If you don't have that password communication, or the credentials are rejected outright, the Help Desk will need to reset things for you at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

Sources: Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — LMS category: "How to login to LMS" and "Student Email / Mcampus Email / Corporate Email".

observations.question: I cant acces moddle, how do I sine in?
observations.answer:
No worries — Moodle (the LMS) doesn't have its own separate password, which is the part that trips most people up. You sign in with your Amref email account. Here's the full process:

1. **Open the LMS.** In your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), type **lms.amref.ac.ke**, or search Google for "lms amref".
2. **Click 'Login/Register'** at the top right of the homepage.
3. **In the pop-up window, click "Use your Amref email address to sign in".** This is the key step — choosing this option hands you over to the Amref account system rather than asking for a Moodle-specific password.
4. **You'll be redirected to the AMREF email login page.** Enter your Amref email address and password. Your address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your university email details.
5. **Complete two-step verification.** The email account has this enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number and then the code sent to you by text. Without this, the login won't finish.
6. **You'll land on the dashboard.** On the left navigation, go to **"My courses"** and select the course you want to study — for example, "Induction Module".

The screenshots below show the login page and dashboard so you can confirm you're on the right screens.

A couple of things worth knowing:

- Your Amref email must be **activated** before it will work — and logging into it once *is* the activation. If you've never logged into your student email at all, that first sign-in is what switches it on.
- If you're thinking of the password reset at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**, note that this resets your **Student Portal** password, not your email/LMS sign-in — they're separate.
- If you never received your email credentials, or the verification code doesn't arrive on your phone, contact the Help Desk at **https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke** so they can reissue your details.

Happy learning!

**Sources:** "How to login to LMS" (LMS category) and "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category), Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — the portal has a self-service reset, so you can do this yourself in a few minutes.

**Resetting your Student Portal password**

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"** on the login screen.
2. Key in your **Amref student email** and the **characters displayed** on screen. The characters confirm you're a real person, and the email tells the portal which account to reset. Your student email takes the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you via text**. This is the identity check, so use the number you can receive the SMS on right away.
4. **Type in your new password and confirm it**, then click **Finish**. Both fields must match or the reset won't complete.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** — that confirms the reset actually took effect.

**Your new password must meet these rules, or it will be rejected:**

- **Length:** a minimum of 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

The screenshots below show these screens as you'll see them.

If the text code never arrives or the reset won't go through, log it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can check your account details.

**Sources**
- *Reset your student portal password* (Knowledgebase)
- *Student Portal* — https://students.amref.ac.ke/
- *LMS – Student Email* (email address format)

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:
Setting up two‑factor authentication on your Office 365 (university email) account is done during a normal sign‑in — Microsoft prompts you for the extra security details itself, so there's no separate enrolment page to hunt for. Here's the full process.

**Before you start**
- Have your university account details to hand: your corporate/University email address (on the **campus.amref.ac.ke** domain) and the password, both of which are sent individually to each student by email.
- Have your mobile phone with you, because verification is completed either through an authenticator app or by a code sent to your phone.

**Enrolling for 2FA**

1. **Sign in to Microsoft 365** with your work or school account and password, exactly as you normally would. Once you choose **Sign in**, the system will prompt you for "more information" — this prompt is the start of the 2FA enrolment.
2. **Choose Next** on that prompt to begin setting up your additional verification method.
3. **Choose Next** again to move to the method selection screen.
4. The **default authentication method is the free Microsoft Authenticator app**. If it's already installed on your mobile device, select **Next** and follow the on‑screen prompts to add your account to the app. If you don't have it installed, the same screen provides a **download link** for the app — install it first, then continue with the prompts.
5. Complete the prompts to finish registering the account. From then on, each sign‑in will require your password plus the second factor — either an approval/code from the authenticator app or **a code sent to the phone number you registered**, which you enter to complete the login.

**Checking it worked:** sign out and sign back in to your email. If you're asked to approve the sign‑in or to enter a code sent to your phone, 2FA is active on the account. You can reach your mailbox from the LMS by going to **Student Services → Student Email**.

The screenshots below show these sign‑in and verification screens as you'll see them.

One caveat: what to do if you lose or replace the phone you registered isn't covered in the Help Desk articles, so if that happens, log a request with the Help Desk so your verification method can be reset.

Sources: Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base — *Microsoft 365 additional verification / Microsoft Authenticator setup* (Knowledgebase) and *Student Email access* (LMS). Further assistance: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
Switching phones is one of the most common reasons Authenticator suddenly locks you out — the app registration lives on the old handset, so your account needs to be re-registered on the new one. Here's how to get back in.

**Re-register Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. **Install the app first.** On your new phone, download **Microsoft Authenticator** from the Google Play Store or App Store. Doing this before you start signing in saves you being stranded mid-way through the prompts.
2. **Start the sign-in.** Key in your username / **AmIU email address**, then enter your password.
3. **Choose Next** when the additional-security-verification page appears. Because your new phone isn't registered yet, Microsoft treats you like a first-time user and walks you through setting the app up again — there's also a download link on that page if you skipped step 1.
4. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and scan the QR code** shown on your computer screen. This is the step that actually binds your account to the new device.
5. Once the scan succeeds, **click Next**, then **click Next** again on the confirmation screen.
6. **Enter your country code and your phone number**, then click **Next**. This adds a fallback verification method to your account.
7. **You'll receive a code from Microsoft by SMS.** Enter the code and click **Next**, then **Next** once more to finish. You should see the confirmation that your account has been set up successfully — that's your verified result.

The screenshots below show these setup screens if you'd like to match them as you go.

**A couple of things worth knowing**

- If you'd prefer not to use the app at all, select **I want to set up a different method** during the process — Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send a 6-digit SMS code to verify your device. That said, an authenticator app is the faster and more secure option, so it's the recommended route.
- Once the new phone is registered, you generally won't be asked for the verification code daily — normally only the first time you sign in to a new app or device, or after you change your password.

**One caveat:** if the sign-in screen only offers to send an approval to your *old* phone and never gives you the option to set up a new method, that situation — clearing an old device off your account — isn't covered in the Help Desk articles, and the IT team will need to reset your MFA registration for you. Raise it at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they can unblock you.

*Source: "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and the Microsoft 365 additional-verification article, Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke).*

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Exams with proctoring can feel like a lot to juggle, so here's the whole thing in one place: first you register on SMOWL, then you sit the exam in VAS.

## Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this first)

SMOWL is the proctoring software that verifies your identity, so your registration must be complete **before** the exam opens.

1. **Register at least 72 hours before exams start.** SMOWL needs time to process your captured images, so leaving this to the last minute risks being locked out of your paper.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** — the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) portal, which holds the SMOWL registration link.
3. **Enter your email address and password** when prompted to log in.
4. Click the **"My Courses"** button, then click your preferred exam.
5. Click to open **CAT** or **Final Exams**. This is what takes you through to the SMOWL registration page.
6. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, so your registration is matched to your student record.
7. **Allow camera access** when your browser asks, so SMOWL can capture your image. This step is essential — without webcam access SMOWL cannot create the reference images it uses to confirm it is you sitting the exam.

## Part 2 — Sit the exam

1. Use the **Google Chrome** browser for the best experience.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and select your exam in VAS.
3. Click to open **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
4. Work through the paper as normal. SMOWL runs in the background **recording all your activities during the exam session**, so stay in front of your webcam and keep to the exam window.
5. When you are done, click **"Submit and Finish"** to end the exam. Your attempt is not complete until you do this.

The screenshots below show these VAS screens so you can match what you see.

One gap worth flagging: the intermediate on-screen prompts between opening the paper and submitting it (the middle steps of the exam session) aren't spelled out in the documentation I have. If you hit something unexpected mid-exam, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke rather than closing the browser.

**Sources**
- *How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* — VAS-Exam system
- *Taking Examination With the SMOWL (Screen Monitoring)* — VAS-Exam system
- VAS portal: https://vas.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I take an exam with webcam monitoring?
observations.answer:
Webcam monitoring during your exams is handled by **SMOWL**, the proctoring software used with Amref's Virtual Assessment System (VAS). There are two parts to it: a one-time registration that teaches SMOWL to recognise your face, and then the permissions you grant when you actually open the exam. Here's the whole process.

## Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this at least 72 hours before exams start)

1. Go to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and open the **SMOWL registration link** there. Registering early matters — the 72-hour window gives the system time to process your captured image, and leaving it to exam day risks being locked out.
2. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, since that's the identity your exam sessions are matched against.
3. **Allow camera access** when your browser prompts you, so SMOWL can capture your image. This captured photo is the reference it later compares against your webcam feed during the exam, so this step can't be skipped.
4. **Download and install the SMOWL software.** Before you do, confirm your machine meets the requirements:
   - Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+
   - A stable internet connection
5. Open your **Downloads** folder, run the installer, and complete the installation.
6. Finish the registration to confirm you're enrolled on the SMOWL platform.

## Part 2 — Sitting the monitored exam

1. When it's time to sit the paper, click to open your **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
2. **Allow SMOWL to open and accept the permissions.** On the pre-test page, first enable **webcam and microphone permissions in your browser**, then tick the **checkbox that allows SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam**, and finally select **Open SMOWL**. If you skip the checkbox, SMOWL won't launch alongside the exam and your session may not be validly proctored.
3. Sit the exam as normal — SMOWL records your activity throughout the session, so stay in view of the camera.
4. When you're done, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

The screenshots below show these VAS and SMOWL screens, which is handy for confirming you're on the right page at each stage.

A couple of caveats: my documentation covers the registration steps and the permission/submission steps above, but the finer detail of what happens between launching SMOWL and submitting (for example specific pre-test identity checks) isn't spelled out — if something on screen doesn't match what's described here, raise it with the Help Desk rather than guessing. And if you've already missed the 72-hour registration deadline, contact the Help Desk straight away instead of waiting for exam day.

**Source:** VAS-Exam system — *How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* (VAS portal: https://vas.amref.ac.ke). For anything not covered here: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — your university (corporate) email is reached through the LMS, and it needs to be activated first.

**Your email address and password**

1. Check the communication that was sent to you individually — it contains your corporate/University email address and the password for the account. Passwords are sent on email, so that message is the only place you'll find yours.
2. Your address follows this format: **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** — for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`. Knowing the pattern helps you confirm you're typing the right address.

**Activating and logging in**

3. Log in to the LMS, go to **Student Services**, and select **Student Email**. This is the entry point to your mailbox (see the LMS screenshots below).
4. Enter your email address and the password from the communication. Note that **logging in is the activation** — until you sign in that first time, the account isn't active and can't be used to reach campus resources.
5. Complete the two-step verification. The account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number; a code is sent to that number, and entering it finishes the login.

Once you're in, you're fully set up — this same email address is also what you use for things like resetting your student portal password at https://students.amref.ac.ke/#.

A couple of things to watch for: if you never received the message with your address and password, or the phone number on file for the verification code isn't yours, those can't be fixed from your side — raise a ticket with the Help Desk and you'll get an email confirming your request, plus notifications as it's worked on.

Sources: "LMS – Student Email" and "Reset your student portal password" (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base). For anything not resolved above, the Help Desk is at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: Where do I sign in to my corporate Outlook account?
observations.answer:
Happy to point you in the right direction — your corporate mailbox is reached through the LMS, so here's the full path from your browser to your inbox.

**Signing in to your corporate (Outlook) email**

1. **Open the LMS.** Type `lms.amref.ac.ke` into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. **Click 'Login/Register'** at the top right of the homepage.
3. **In the pop-up window, click "Use your Amref email address to sign in."** This hands you over to Microsoft rather than asking for a separate LMS password.
4. **Enter your Amref email address and password** on the AMREF email login page you're redirected to. You'll land on your LMS dashboard — the screenshots below show these login screens.
5. **Under Student Services on the LMS, select Student Email.** That's the doorway to your corporate/university mailbox.
6. **Sign in with your corporate address and password.** The address format is `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually by email along with your address — every student receives their own details.
7. **Complete two-step verification.** The account has two-step verification enabled, so after your password you'll be prompted for more information — choose **Next**, supply the phone number where the code should be sent, then enter the code you receive to finish signing in.

A couple of things worth knowing:

- **Your first successful login is what activates the account** — until you log in, the mailbox isn't active, so don't skip this even if you don't need to read mail yet.
- If you never received the email containing your corporate address and password, you won't be able to get past step 6 — raise that with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so your details can be reissued.

Sources: "How to login to LMS" (LMS category) and "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS category), plus the Knowledgebase article on additional verification when signing in to Microsoft 365 — all available via the Amref Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: I cannot log in to my Amref systems. Can you help me?
observations.answer:
I'm sorry you're locked out — let's get you back in. Since "Amref systems" covers a few different logins, here's the full path for each one, starting with your university email because that account is the key that unlocks the LMS.

## 1. Activate your Amref (university) email first

Your email account only becomes usable once you log into it — **logging in = activation**.

1. Your email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke).
2. The password was sent to you individually — the communication you received contains both your corporate/University email address and the account password.
3. When you log in, you'll be asked for your phone number, because the account has **two-step verification** enabled. A code is sent to that number, and you must enter it to complete the login.
4. You can reach this mailbox from the LMS: under **Student Services**, select **Student Email**.

If you've never received those credentials, that's the point to raise with the Help Desk — nothing else will work until the account is active.

## 2. Log in to the LMS (Moodle / e-learning)

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer, or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. At the **top right** of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
3. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — this is what routes you to the university's sign-in system rather than a separate LMS password.
4. You'll be redirected to the AMREF email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password there.
5. Once authenticated, you land on your dashboard. On the **left navigation** panel, go to **My courses** and select the course you want to study (for example, "Induction module").

Because the LMS uses your email credentials, an LMS login failure is almost always an email account issue — so fix step 1 before troubleshooting here.

## 3. Reset your Student Portal password

If the portal is where you're stuck:

1. Go to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**
2. Click **"Forgot your password"**.
3. Enter your **Amref student email** and the characters displayed on screen.
4. Enter your **phone number**, then the code sent to you by text — this confirms it's really you.
5. Type your new password, confirm it, and click **finish**.
6. Return to the portal and log in with your student email and the new password.

Your new password must be:
- **At least 10 characters** long;
- A mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters;
- Not any of your official names.

The screenshots below show these login and reset screens so you can match what's on your device.

**One caveat:** if the code never arrives by text during either the email two-step verification or the portal reset, the phone number on your record may be wrong or out of date — that has to be corrected by the Help Desk, and isn't something you can change yourself.

If you can tell me which system is failing and what message you see (wrong password, no verification code, "account not found"), I can narrow this down for you.

---
**Sources:** "How to login to LMS" (LMS), "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Corporate Email; Official Email" (LMS), and "Reset your student portal password" (Knowledgebase) — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base. For account issues that need staff action: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

2. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"**. This redirects you to the Amref email login page, because the LMS authenticates you through your Amref account rather than a separate Moodle password.
3. Enter your **Amref email address and password**, and you'll land on your dashboard.
4. On the **left navigation tool of the dashboard**, click **"My courses"**. This lists every course you're enrolled in — for example, "Induction Module".
5. **Click the course** you need. Its assignments and other activities are inside the course page, so opening the course is what makes them visible to you. The screenshots below show what this looks like on screen.

A couple of things worth checking while you're there:

- If **"My courses" is empty or the course you need isn't listed**, the issue is enrolment rather than login — the assignments won't show because the course itself hasn't been attached to your account yet.
- Also make sure you're signed in with your official student email in the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke**, since that's the account tied to your campus resources.

Beyond that, the Help Desk Knowledge Base doesn't document assignment-specific faults — things like an assignment link that's visible but won't open, a greyed-out submission button, or a submission window that has closed. If that's what you're seeing, or if your course list is empty, please raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can check your enrolment and the course settings directly. If you can tell me exactly what you see when you open the course, I'm happy to narrow it down further.

observations.question: How do I use Microsoft Teams for my classes?
observations.answer:
Good news — you don't need a separate Teams account: your AMIU email already gives you access. Here's how to get in and start using it for class.

**1. Use your AMIU-issued email address as your Teams login.**
That single account unlocks the Microsoft Office suite — Outlook (email), Word, Excel, Stream, PowerPoint, Teams, Notebook, Forms, OneDrive, OneNote, To-Do, Visio, Whiteboard and Yammer — so there's nothing extra to register for.

**2. Install the Teams app on the device you'll study on.**
Download it from https://www.microsoft.com/en-ww/microsoft-teams/download-app and install it on your laptop, tablet or mobile phone. Installing it means class notifications and meeting joins come straight to your device.

**3. Or use Teams in your browser instead.**
Go to https://login.microsoft.com and sign in there — useful if you're on a shared or borrowed computer where you can't install software.

**4. Sign in with the email credentials you received.**
Enter your AMIU email address and password exactly as they were issued to you.

**5. Complete the extra verification step if you're prompted.**
After you choose **Sign in**, Microsoft 365 will ask you for more information — choose **Next**. observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Resetting your student portal password is a quick self‑service process — here's the full path from the login page to a working login.

**Steps**

1. Open the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and, on the login page, click **Forgot your password?**
2. Key in your **Amref student email** and the **characters displayed** on screen. Use your official university address (the format is firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke) — the portal matches the reset request against the email held on your student record, so a personal address won't be recognised.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you via text**. This is the identity check, so it must be the number registered on your student record for the code to reach you.
4. Type in your **new password**, **confirm** it, and click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** — this last step confirms the reset actually took effect rather than just appearing to.

**Your new password must meet these rules,** or it will be rejected at step 4:

- **Length:** a minimum of 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

The screenshots below show the reset screens so you can confirm you're on the right page at each stage.

A couple of things worth knowing: if the text code never arrives, it usually means the phone number on your student record differs from the one you're entering — that has to be corrected on your record before the reset can complete, so log it with the Help Desk. Note too that your portal password is separate from your student email password; resetting one does not change the other.

**Source:** "Reset your student portal password" and "Student Portal" — Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base. Portal link: https://students.amref.ac.ke/ · Further support: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:
Setting up two‑factor authentication on your Office 365 (Microsoft 365) account is done the first time you sign in and get prompted for extra security information. Here's the full process.

**Enrolling in 2FA with Microsoft Authenticator**

1. **Install the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone first** (if you can). It's free, and having it ready before you start means you can complete enrolment in one sitting rather than being interrupted mid‑way.
2. **Sign in to Microsoft 365 with your work/school account and password** exactly as you normally do. This is your University corporate email address (the **campus.amref.ac.ke** account) together with the password that was sent to you individually by email.
3. After you choose **Sign in**, you'll be **prompted for more information** — this is the 2FA enrolment prompt appearing because your account requires a second verification step beyond the password.
4. **Choose Next.**
5. The **default authentication method is the free Microsoft Authenticator app**. If you already have it installed on your mobile device, select **Next** and **follow the prompts to add this account**. If it isn't installed, **use the download link provided on that screen** to get it, then continue.
6. Because your University email account has **two‑step verification enabled**, you'll also be asked to **enter your phone number**, and a **code will be sent to that number** to complete the login. Use a number you have with you, since you'll need to read the code off that phone.
7. To confirm everything works, reach your mailbox the normal way: on the **LMS**, go to **Student Services** and select **Student Email**. If your inbox opens after the verification step, your enrolment is done.

The screenshots below show these sign‑in and verification screens so you can match what's on your own screen.

A couple of things worth knowing: keep the phone you enrol reachable, because that device (or the Authenticator app on it) becomes your second factor for every future sign‑in. If you never received the email carrying your campus.amref.ac.ke address and password, you can't start step 2 at all — that has to be reissued to you before enrolment is possible.

**Sources**
- Knowledgebase — Microsoft 365 additional verification / Microsoft Authenticator setup article
- LMS — Student Email access article

If the prompts on your screen differ from the above, or your verification code never arrives, log it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
Switching phones does break Authenticator, because the account approval sits on the old device — the fix is to re-register the app on your new handset by walking through the setup flow again.

**Re-registering Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. **Install the app on the new phone first.** Download **Microsoft Authenticator** from the Google Play Store or the App Store. Having it ready means you won't stall halfway through the sign-in prompt.
2. **Start a sign-in.** Key in your username/AmIU email address, then enter your password. Because your new phone is an unrecognised device, Microsoft will ask for additional verification — this is expected behaviour, not a fault with your account.
3. **When the setup page appears, choose Next.** The default method offered is the free Microsoft Authenticator app; if you hadn't installed it, this page also gives you a download link.
4. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on the new phone and scan the QR code** shown on your computer screen. This is the step that binds your AmIU account to the new device.
5. **Once the scan succeeds, click Next**, then **Next** again on the confirmation screen.
6. **Enter your country code and phone number, then click Next.** This registers a backup verification number, which is what saves you next time you change devices.
7. **Microsoft sends a code by SMS to that number.** Enter the code and click **Next**, then **Next** once more.
8. You'll get a confirmation that your account is set up — sign in once more to verify that the approval prompt now arrives on the new phone.

**If you'd rather verify by text than by app:** at the setup page select **I want to set up a different method**, give your mobile number, and Microsoft 365 will send a 6-digit SMS code to verify the device. Do note the recommendation to stick with the authenticator app — it's faster and more secure than SMS.

Once this is done, you shouldn't be prompted for the extra verification day to day — normally only the first time you sign in on a new app or device, or after changing your password.

The screenshots below show the setup screens you'll pass through.

One caveat: this works when the sign-in actually offers you the setup/QR-code page. If instead it insists on approving a notification on your **old** phone and gives you no way to add a new method, that account-reset path isn't documented in the knowledge base — in that case ask the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke to clear your existing MFA registration so you can re-enrol with the steps above.

**Sources:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" (Knowledgebase) and the Knowledgebase article on Microsoft 365 additional verification methods. Help Desk: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I take an exam with webcam monitoring?
observations.answer:
Webcam‑monitored exams at Amref run on the VAS‑Exam system with SMOWL proctoring, and there are two parts to it: a one‑off SMOWL registration you must complete **before** exam week, and then the launch sequence on the day of the exam. Here's the whole thing end to end.

## Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this at least 72 hours before exams start)

1. Go to the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and log in. This is where your CATs and final exams live, and it's also where the SMOWL registration link sits.
2. Click the **SMOWL registration link** in the VAS portal. This takes you to the SMOWL registration page.
3. Enter your details — your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address exactly, because that's the identity SMOWL ties your captured images to; a personal email won't match you to your exam.
4. **Allow camera access** when the browser prompts you, so SMOWL can capture your reference image. This baseline photo is what the system later compares you against during the exam, so registration can't complete without it.
5. **Download and install the SMOWL software.** Check your Downloads folder for the installer and run it. Your machine needs to meet the requirements: **Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+**, plus a stable internet connection.
6. Finish the registration to confirm your enrolment on the SMOWL platform.

**Don't leave this to the last minute — registration is required at least 72 hours before exams begin**, so that your details and image are processed before your first paper opens.

## Part 2 — On exam day

1. Log back in to the VAS portal and click to open your **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
2. Allow **SMOWL to open** and accept the permissions it requests.
3. On the **pre‑test page**, grant your browser's **webcam and microphone** permissions, then tick the **checkbox that allows SMOWL to run** directly at the start of the exam. Finally, select the **Open SMOWL** option to launch the proctor.
4. Sit the exam as normal. SMOWL records your activity throughout the session, so stay in frame and keep the proctoring window running until you're done.
5. When you've finished, click **"Submit and finish"** to close and submit the exam.

The screenshots below show these VAS/SMOWL screens, which will help you recognise the pre‑test page and the permission prompts when you get to them.

One gap I should flag honestly: the material I have details the launch sequence at steps 2–3 and the finish at step 6, but the intermediate on‑screen checks (such as any identity capture step immediately before the questions open) aren't spelled out. If you hit a screen you're unsure about mid‑exam, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke rather than closing the window, as leaving the exam can interrupt the proctoring record.

**Source:** *VAS‑Exam system — How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* (VAS portal: https://vas.amref.ac.ke)

observations.question: I cannot log in to my Amref systems. Can you help me?
observations.answer:
I'm sorry you're locked out — that's stressful, especially around deadlines. Since "Amref systems" covers a few different logins that share one set of credentials, here's how each one works, starting with the account everything else depends on.

## 1. Start with your Amref (university) email — it's the master key

Your LMS login redirects to the Amref email sign-in page, so if your email account isn't working, nothing else will let you in either.

1. Check your email address format: **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke).
2. Your password was sent to you individually — the communication you received contains both your corporate/University email address and the account password. Use those exact details.
3. **Your email must be ACTIVATED before it will work anywhere, and logging in *is* the activation.** If you have never signed in to it even once, that's very often the reason other logins fail.
4. The email account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number and then a code sent to it to complete the login. Have your phone with you and make sure the number on file is one you can currently receive texts on.
5. To reach the mailbox, go to the LMS, open **Student Services**, and select **Student Email**.

## 2. Logging in to the LMS

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. At the top right of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
3. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — this is the step people miss, because the LMS doesn't use a separate password of its own.
4. You'll be redirected to the Amref email login page. Enter your Amref email address and password, and you'll be taken to your dashboard.
5. From the left navigation menu on the dashboard, go to **My courses** and select the course you want, e.g. "Induction module".

The screenshot below shows what the LMS login screens look like, so you can confirm you're on the right page.

## 3. Logging in to the Student Portal (registration, transcripts, fees)

1. Go to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**.
2. If you've forgotten the password, click **forgot your password**.
3. Enter your Amref student email and the characters displayed on screen.
4. Enter your phone number, then the code sent to you via text — so again, keep your phone handy.
5. Type your new password, confirm it, and click **finish**.
6. Return to the portal and log in with your student email and the new password.

Your new password must be at least **10 characters**, mix uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters, and must not be any of your official names — the portal will reject it otherwise, which can look like a failed reset.

## If you're still stuck

If the phone number holding your verification code is out of date, or you never received the email containing your original password, that can't be fixed from your side — raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke so they can reissue your details.

It would also help me narrow things down if you tell me which system is failing and what the error says — LMS, Student Portal, or your email — and I'll walk you through that one specifically.

observations.question: How do I use Microsoft Teams for my classes?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — Teams is where you'll do document sharing, online meetings, private and group chats, and virtual classrooms, and your AMIU account already covers it.

**Getting into Microsoft Teams**

1. **Have your AMIU-issued email address and password ready.** That account is what unlocks the Microsoft Office suite for you — Outlook (email), Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Stream, Teams, Notebook, Forms, OneDrive, OneNote, To-Do, Visio, Whiteboard and Yammer — so you don't need a separate Teams sign-up.
2. **Install the Teams app on the device you'll use for class** — laptop, tablet or mobile phone — from https://www.microsoft.com/en-ww/microsoft-teams/download-app. Installing it (rather than only using the browser) tends to give the smoothest experience for meetings on a phone or tablet.
3. **Or use Teams in your browser** by going to https://login.microsoft.com if you'd rather not install anything.
4. **Sign in with the email credentials you received** from the university — the same email address and password you use for your AMIU email.
5. **Complete the extra verification if you're prompted for it.** After you enter your password, Microsoft may ask for more information; choose **Next**. The default method is the free **Microsoft Authenticator** app — if it's already on your mobile device, select **Next** and follow the prompts to add your account; if it isn't installed, use the download link shown on that screen first. This second step is what confirms it's really you signing in, so don't skip past it.
6. **Once you're in, use Teams for your coursework** — join your online class meetings, chat privately or in groups with classmates and lecturers, and share documents.

The screenshots below show the relevant screens if you'd like to compare as you go.

One thing to flag: how your lecturer shares each specific class team or meeting link (for example whether it's posted in the LMS or emailed to you) isn't documented in the material I have. If you've signed in successfully but can't find your class, check with your lecturer or raise it at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources**
- LMS Knowledge Base — *Microsoft Teams* (download and web access instructions)
- Knowledge Base — *Signing in to Microsoft 365 with additional verification (Microsoft Authenticator)*

observations.question: Hello, how can I contact the AmIU Help Desk?
observations.answer:
Happy to help — there are three ways to reach the AmIU Help Desk, and submitting a ticket is the route that gets your issue logged and tracked.

**Option 1 — From the LMS (recommended, since you're already signed in)**

1. Log in to the LMS and hover over the **"Student Services"** menu on the top navigation.
2. Click the **Help Desk** link in the drop-down. The AmIU Help Desk page will launch (see the screenshots below).

**Option 2 — Straight to the Help Desk site**

1. Visit **http://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke** in your browser — this opens the same Help Desk page without going through the LMS.

**Option 3 — By email**

1. Send your query to **helpdesk@amref.ac.ke**. A ticket is created and assigned to you automatically, so you don't need to fill in the online form.

**Submitting a ticket on the Help Desk page**

1. Click the **"Submit a Ticket"** button.
2. Select the **category** that matches the area you need assistance with — this routes your request to the right support staff.
3. On the online form that opens, enter your **name**, **email**, and **admissions/registration number** so the team can identify your record.
4. Select the **priority** of the issue, enter a **subject**, and write a clear **message** describing the assistance you need — the more specific you are, the fewer clarifying emails are needed.
5. **Attach any files** that help illustrate the problem (screenshots, documents), if you have any.
6. Click **"Submit Ticket"**.

**What happens next:** your ticket goes to the university Help Desk staff, and you'll receive an email confirming the request was received. Every time a change is made to your ticket, you'll get an email notification — so keep an eye on the inbox for the address you entered on the form.

Source: "How to access the AmIU help desk" (Knowledgebase) — http://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I log in to the LMS?
observations.answer:
I can see you're trying to log in to the LMS, and that can be frustrating. Let's walk through the steps to get you in.

To log in to the LMS, follow these steps:

1. Open your browser and type in [lms.amref.ac.ke](http://lms.amref.ac.ke) or search Google for "lms amref". You can use any browser like Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer, or Opera Mini.

2. At the top right of the homepage, click on the 'Login/Register' button. This will open a pop-up window.

3. In the pop-up window, click on the "Use your Amref email address to sign in" button. You will be redirected to the AMREF email login page.

4. On the AMREF email login page, enter your Amref email address and password. This is the same email and password you use for your Amref account.

5. After entering your email and password, you will be taken to the dashboard. From the left navigation tool, navigate to "My courses" and pick the course for which you wish to study.

That's it! You should now be logged in to the LMS and ready to start your course.

**Important note:** Make sure you have activated your student email account before logging in to the LMS, as it is required for the login process. You can activate your student email account by following the instructions in the email you received from the university.
