observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
I can see you're having trouble resetting your student portal password. 

To reset your password, follow these steps:

1. Go to the student portal on https://students.amref.ac.ke/ and click on 'forgot your password' if you've forgotten it. 
2. Key in your Amref student email and the characters displayed in the security image.
3. Key in your phone number, and a code will be sent to you via text. 
4. Type in the code sent via text and click next.
5. Type in your new password and confirm it, then finish.
6. Go back to the portal to log in with your student email and new password.

Please note that your password should have a minimum of 10 characters, a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and should not be any of your official names.

If you're having trouble accessing your student email, which is required to reset your portal password, please see the details below. 

The student email is in the format of firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke, and the password is sent to you via email. You need to activate the email by logging in with the provided password. 

To access your student email, go to the LMS under Student Services, select Student Email, and follow the on-screen instructions.

Caveats: Make sure you have access to your phone number and the email account associated with your Amref student email. If you're having trouble with your student email, please contact the relevant authorities for assistance.

Source: Reset your student portal password, Student Portal, and LMS.

observations.question: My Student Portal login is not working. What should I do?
observations.answer:

If you're still having trouble, please contact the Help Desk for further assistance.

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:

To set up Microsoft Authenticator, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Microsoft Authenticator setup page. Although the exact URL is not provided in the context, you can search for "Microsoft Authenticator setup" in your browser or click on the link provided in your university's Microsoft 365 account.
2. Key in your Amref International University email address (your username) and enter your password. This will redirect you to a page that requires you to download the Microsoft Authenticator app.
3. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone from the Google Store or App Store.
4. Open the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone and click on "Next".
5. Scan the QR code displayed on the Microsoft Authenticator setup page using your phone's camera.
6. Once successful, click on "Next" again.
7. Enter your country code and phone number, and click on "Next".
8. You will receive a code from Microsoft on your mobile phone. Enter the code and click on "Next".
9. Click on "Next" again to complete the setup process.
10. Congratulations! You have successfully set up your Microsoft Authenticator account.

Please note that setting up Microsoft Authenticator requires a mobile device with a working internet connection. Also, make sure you have the correct country code and phone number to receive the verification code.

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:
I can sense your frustration with trying to set up 2FA on Office 365. Let's walk through the enrollment process step by step.

To enroll for 2FA on Office 365, you'll need to set up the Microsoft Authenticator app and link it to your account. Here's how:

1. First, sign in to Microsoft 365 with your work or school account using your password. You can do this by going to the Microsoft 365 login page and entering your credentials. **Please note that you won't be able to access your account without your password, so make sure you have it handy.**
2. After signing in, you'll be prompted to choose your authentication method. Since you're trying to set up 2FA, choose the option to use the free Microsoft Authenticator app.
3. If you have the Microsoft Authenticator app installed on your mobile device, select Next and follow the prompts to add this account. If you don't have it installed, there's a link provided to download it. You can download the app from the App Store (for iOS devices) or Google Play Store (for Android devices).
4. Once you've downloaded and installed the app, open it and follow the prompts to add your Office 365 account. You'll need to enter your email address and password to link the app to your account.
5. After adding your account, you'll need to set up 2FA by entering a verification code sent to your phone. This code will be used to complete the login process.

That's it! You've successfully set up 2FA on Office 365 using the Microsoft Authenticator app.

**Please note that if you're having trouble accessing your email, you may need to check your corporate/University email address and password, which are sent to you individually via email.**

observations.question: What is SMOWL proctoring and how do I use it?

2. To use SMOWL, lecturers need to set up the exam proctoring software, which involves creating a unique exam link and sharing it with students. This link is used by students to access the online exam.
3. During the exam, SMOWL records the student's screen and webcam, allowing lecturers to monitor the student's activity and ensure they are not cheating.
4. If you are a lecturer, you can find more information on how to set up and use SMOWL in the recorded training session on lecturer exam proctoring using SMOWL (Lecturer Exams Proctoring training).
5. If you are a student, you will need to access the online exam through the unique link provided by your lecturer. Make sure you have a stable internet connection and a suitable device to ensure a smooth exam experience.

**Please note that SMOWL proctoring is a secure and confidential process, and any attempt to cheat or compromise the exam will be detected and addressed accordingly.**

observations.question: smwol camera not workng during my exam
observations.answer:

To resolve the SMOWL camera not working during your exam, follow these steps:

1. Ensure you have allowed SMOWL to access your webcam. Before the exam starts, you should have allowed SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam by clicking the checkbox and selecting the Open SMOWL option. If you haven't done this, go back to the CAT or Final Exams page, allow SMOWL to open, and accept the permissions. **Please note that failing to do this will prevent SMOWL from accessing your webcam.**
2. Check if your webcam is enabled and working properly. Make sure your browser is configured to allow camera access, and your webcam is properly connected to your device.
3. Ensure your system meets the SMOWL software requirements: Windows 10 and 11 / MacOS 10.15+, and a stable internet connection.
4. If you have already installed the SMOWL software, check if it is up to date. You can check the downloads file and install any updates.
5. Complete the SMOWL registration process by entering your details, including your Amref (mcampus) email address, and allowing camera access to capture your image.
6. Once you have completed the registration process, restart your browser and attempt to access the SMOWL system again.
7. If the issue persists, try downloading and installing the SMOWL software again, ensuring that your system meets the requirements.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the issue with the SMOWL camera not working during your exam.

Please note that SMOWL will be monitoring and recording all your activities during the exam session, so ensure you are in a quiet and private space.

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:

observations.question: How do I log in to the LMS?
observations.answer:
Logging into the LMS uses your Amref email account as the sign-in method, so the whole process is really two things: getting to the LMS login prompt, then authenticating with your university email credentials. Here's the full sequence.

**Before you start:** your Amref email account must be activated, because the LMS hands you over to it for sign-in. Logging in to the email for the first time *is* the activation. Your address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password was sent to you individually in the communication containing your corporate/University email address.

**Steps:**

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini work), or search Google for "lms amref" and follow the result.
2. On the LMS homepage, look to the **top right** and click **'Login/Register'**.
3. In the pop-up window that appears, click the **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** button — this is what routes you to the university's single sign-on rather than a separate LMS password.
4. You'll be redirected to the **AMREF email login page**. Enter your Amref email address and password here.
5. Complete the **two-step verification** — the email account has this enabled, so you'll be asked for a phone number, and a code will be sent to it. Enter the code to finish the login.
6. You'll land on your LMS **dashboard**. On the **left navigation** panel, go to **"My courses"** and select the course you want to study (for example, "Induction module").

The screenshots below show the login page and dashboard at these stages, so you can check you're on the right screen at each point.

A couple of things worth knowing: if your password isn't working, check that you're using the one sent to you in your account communication, since the LMS accepts nothing but your email credentials at step 4. And keep your phone to hand — without it you can't clear the two-step verification prompt at step 5. If you're still locked out after that, the Help Desk can verify your account details.

**Sources (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, LMS category):**
- "How to login to LMS"
- "Student Email; Mcampus Email; Cooporate Email; Official Email"

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — the portal has a self-service reset, so you can do this yourself in a couple of minutes.

**Resetting your Student Portal password**

1. Open the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **Forgot your password?** on the login screen.
2. Key in your **Amref student email** and the **characters displayed** on screen. The email identifies your account, and the characters confirm a real person is making the request.
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you via text**. This is the verification step that proves the account is yours before any password change is allowed.
4. Type in your **new password**, confirm it, then click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and **log in with your student email and the new password** — that confirms the reset actually took effect.

**Your new password must meet these rules, or it will be rejected:**

- **Length:** a minimum of 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not** be any of your official names.

A couple of things worth knowing: the email you enter at step 2 is your university/student email in the format *firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke* (for example test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke). Also note the text code in step 3 goes to the phone number tied to your account, so if no message arrives, that's the point to raise with the Help Desk rather than retrying repeatedly.

The screenshots below show the reset screens as you'll see them.

If the reset doesn't complete — the email isn't recognised, or the SMS code never arrives — log it with the Amref Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they can verify your details on file.

- *Student Portal* — https://students.amref.ac.ke/

observations.question: How do I set up Microsoft Authenticator?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through it — this is a one-time setup that adds a second layer of security to your AmIU Microsoft 365 account, so that after your password you also confirm a code from your phone.

**Before you start:** have your phone with you, and be ready to install the free Microsoft Authenticator app from the Google Play Store or the App Store.

1. Go to the Microsoft 365 sign-in page and key in your username / AmIU email address.
2. Enter your password and choose **Sign in**, exactly as you normally do. As a first-time user you'll be prompted for more information and redirected to a page asking you to set up the Microsoft Authenticator app — this is the step that secures your account.
3. Choose **Next**.
4. When asked for your authentication method, the default is the free **Microsoft Authenticator** app. If it's already installed on your phone, select **Next** and follow the prompts to add the account. If it isn't installed, use the download link provided on that page (or get it from the Google Play Store / App Store) before continuing.
5. Click **Next** — a QR code will appear on your computer screen.
6. Open Microsoft Authenticator on your phone and **scan the QR code**. This links your AmIU account to the app so it can generate your verification codes.
7. Once the scan is successful, click **Next**.
8. Click **Next** again to move on to the phone verification step.
9. Enter your **country code** and your **phone number**, then click **Next**. This gives you a backup way to verify if your app is ever unavailable.
10. Microsoft will send a code to your mobile phone. Enter the code and click **Next**.
11. Click **Next** one last time. You should now see confirmation that your account is set up — that's it, your MFA is active.

From here on, each time you sign in you'll enter your password and then approve the request or type the code from the Authenticator app, so **keep the app installed and don't delete the account entry from it** — removing it will lock you out of the verification step.

The screenshots below show what these prompts look like as you move through them.

If something stalls part-way — for example the QR code won't scan or the SMS code never arrives — the specific fix for that isn't documented here, so please raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

Sources: "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and "Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication" — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase.

observations.question: I changed phones and Microsoft Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
Changing phones does break Authenticator, because the account registration lives on the old handset rather than in the app itself — so the fix is to re-register Authenticator on your new phone. Here's how to work through it.

## Re-registering Authenticator on your new phone

1. **Install Microsoft Authenticator on the new phone first** — download it from the Google Play Store or the App Store. Do this before you start signing in, so the app is ready when the QR code appears.
2. **Go to the sign-in page and key in your username / AmIU email address.**
3. **Enter your password.**
4. Because this is effectively a new device registration, you'll be taken to a page prompting you to set up the Microsoft Authenticator app (there's also a download link on that page if you skipped step 1). **Choose Next.**
5. **Open Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone and scan the QR code** shown on your screen. This is the step that binds your account to the new handset.
6. Once the scan is successful, **click Next**, then **click Next** again on the confirmation screen.
7. **Enter your country code and your phone number, then click Next.** This registers a phone number as a backup verification route.
8. **Microsoft sends a code by SMS to that number — enter the code and click Next.**
9. **Click Next** to finish. Your account is now set up, and approvals will come to the new phone from here on.

The screenshots below walk through these same setup screens if you'd like to match what you're seeing.

## If you'd rather not use the app

At the setup screen, select **I want to set up a different method** and choose SMS. Microsoft 365 will ask for your mobile number and send a 6-digit code to verify the device. Worth knowing: the guidance recommends the authenticator app over SMS as the faster and more secure option.

## Two things to expect

- You'll normally only be asked for this extra verification the first time you sign in on a new app or device, or after a password change — so this prompt after switching phones is expected behaviour, not a fault.
- **If sign-in never offers you the QR/setup screen and instead just waits for an approval on your old phone, stop there.** Clearing an old device registration isn't covered in the Help Desk articles, so raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they can reset your MFA registration for you.

**Sources:** "Setting up Microsoft Authenticator" and the Microsoft 365 additional-verification setup article, Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase — https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
Exams on the Virtual Assessment System (VAS) have two parts: a one-time SMOWL proctoring registration, then sitting the exam itself. Here's the whole flow from start to finish.

**Part 1 — Register on SMOWL (do this first)**

1. Register **at least 72 hours before your exams start**. SMOWL needs time to process your captured images, so leaving this to the last minute risks being locked out of the exam.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and enter your email address and password when prompted.
3. Click the **"My courses"** button, then click the exam you want.
4. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** item — this is what takes you through to the SMOWL registration page.
5. On the SMOWL page, enter your details: your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, as that is the identity SMOWL ties your proctoring record to.
6. **Allow camera access** when your browser asks, so SMOWL can capture your image. This step is essential — without webcam access SMOWL cannot register you or verify you during the exam.

**Part 2 — Sitting the exam**

1. Use the **Google Chrome** browser for the best experience — other browsers may not handle the proctoring components properly.
2. Go to **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and select your exam in VAS.
3. Click to open the **CAT** or **Final Exams** paper. SMOWL records all your activities throughout the exam session, so keep your webcam unobstructed and stay in front of it.
4. When you have finished answering, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam. Nothing is final until you click this, so don't simply close the browser tab.

The screenshots below show these VAS screens so you can match what you see on your own display.

One caveat: the middle steps of the exam-sitting procedure (what happens between opening the paper and submitting) aren't fully spelled out in the material I have beyond the fact that SMOWL is monitoring throughout. If you hit something unexpected mid-exam, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke rather than exiting the session.

**Sources:**

- "Taking examination With the SMOWL (Screen Monitoring)" — VAS-Exam system

1. Go to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke** and open the SMOWL registration link there. Registration must happen **at least 72 hours before your exams start** — this gives the system time to process your enrolment, so leaving it to exam day risks being locked out.
2. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mcampus) email address**. Use the mcampus address specifically, since that's the identity the exam links your proctoring record to.
3. **Allow camera access** when your browser prompts you, so SMOWL can capture your reference images — these are what your face is later matched against during the exam.
4. **Download and install the SMOWL software.** Check your Downloads folder for the installer and run it. Confirm your device meets the requirements first:
   - Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 10.15+
   - A stable internet connection
5. Complete the registration to finish enrolling.

## Part 2 — Sitting the exam with monitoring on

1. Log in to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke**.
2. Click to open your **CAT** or **Final Exams**.
3. Allow SMOWL to open and **accept the permissions**. On the pre-test page, enable **webcam and microphone permissions in your browser**, then tick the **checkbox to allow SMOWL to run** at the start of the exam, and select **Open SMOWL**. Skipping the checkbox is the usual reason the exam won't start — SMOWL has to be running before the paper opens.
4. Sit the exam as normal. SMOWL records all your activity throughout the session, so stay in front of the camera and keep your internet connection stable.
5. When you're done, click **"Submit and finish"** to end the exam.

The screenshots below show these VAS and SMOWL screens, which helps confirm you're on the right page.

Two caveats: the intermediate on-screen prompts between launching SMOWL and submitting aren't detailed in our documented steps, and neither is what to do if SMOWL fails to launch after you've accepted permissions — if you hit either, contact the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke, ideally before exam day rather than during it.

**Source:** VAS-Exam system — *How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software* (https://vas.amref.ac.ke)

observations.question: How do I access my university email?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this. Your university (corporate) email is reached through the LMS, and the first time you log in that login *is* the activation of the account — so there's no separate activation step to hunt for.

**Steps to access your email**

1. **Find your credentials first.** The details are sent individually to each student, so check the communication you received — it contains your corporate/University email address and the password for the account. Your address follows the format `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`), and the password is sent on email.
2. **Log in to the LMS** with your usual LMS credentials.
3. **Go to Student Services** and select **Student Email**. This is the gateway to your mailbox — the screenshots below show where this sits in the LMS.
4. **Enter your email address** in the `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` format, then the password you were sent.
5. **Complete two-step verification.** The account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll be asked for your phone number and a code will be sent to it — enter that code to finish signing in. Have your phone with you before you start, as you can't complete the login without it.
6. **You're done — and activated.** Because logging in equals activation, once you land in the mailbox your account is live and you can use it to access campus resources.

**A couple of things to watch for:** the two-step verification means a working phone number is essential, so if the code never arrives you'll need Help Desk assistance to sort the number on file. If you no longer have the message containing your email address and password, that also needs to go through the Help Desk — raise a ticket and you'll receive an email confirming your request, plus a notification whenever the ticket is updated.

---
**Sources:** LMS – Student Email (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base, LMS category) and the Help Desk ticket-submission article. No direct article URLs were provided with these entries; for further help, visit https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: Where do I sign in to my corporate Outlook account?

2. **Log in to the LMS** — click **Login/Register** at the top right of the homepage, then in the pop-up window click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"**. This redirects you to the AMREF email login page, where you enter your Amref email address and password before landing on your dashboard.
3. **Go to Student Services → Student Email** — on the LMS, under **Student Services**, select **Student Email**. This is the documented route to your corporate mailbox, so you don't need to hunt for a separate address.
4. **Enter your corporate email address** — the format is `firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke` (for example, `test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke`).
5. **Enter your password** — this was sent to you individually by email; that communication contains both your corporate / University email address and the account password.
6. **Complete the two-step verification** — after you choose **Sign in**, you'll be prompted for more information; choose **Next**. The account has two-step verification enabled, so you'll supply your phone number and a code will be sent to it (codes come either from an authenticator app or to your phone) to finish the login.
7. **You're in.** **Note that logging in for the first time is what activates the account** — until that first successful sign-in, the mailbox isn't active, so don't skip it before you need to use campus resources.

observations.question: I cannot log in to my Amref systems. Can you help me?
observations.answer:
I'm sorry you're locked out — that's stressful, especially if you're mid-term. Since "Amref systems" could mean a few different things, here are the documented login procedures for the three main ones. Your Amref email is the key to most of them, so start there.

## 1. First, make sure your Amref email is active

Almost everything else depends on this, because the LMS signs you in with your Amref email account.

1. Your email address follows the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** (for example, test.student@mcampus.amref.ac.ke).
2. Your password was **sent to you on email** — the details to access the account are sent individually to each student, and that communication contains both your corporate/University email address and your password.
3. The account must be **ACTIVATED before you can use it**, and logging in *is* the activation — so the very first successful sign-in does the job.
4. The account has **two-step verification enabled**, so you'll be asked for a phone number, and a code will be sent to it to complete the login. If you're not receiving that code, the login can't finish — that's a common sticking point.
5. Once you're in the LMS, you can reach your mailbox at any time under **Student Services → Student Email**.

## 2. Logging in to the LMS (Moodle)

1. Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser (Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini), or search Google for "lms amref".
2. At the **top right** of the homepage, click **Login/Register**.
3. In the pop-up window, click **"Use your Amref email address to sign in"** — the LMS doesn't hold a separate password, so this is the only route in.
4. You'll be redirected to the **AMREF email login page**, where you enter your Amref email address and password. After that you land on your dashboard.
5. On the **left navigation** of the dashboard, go to **My courses** and pick the course you want to study (for example, "Induction module").

The screenshots below show these login screens so you can match what you're seeing.

## 3. Resetting your Student Portal password

If it's the Student Portal that's rejecting you, reset the password yourself:

1. Go to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **"Forgot your password"**.
2. Enter your **Amref student email** and the characters displayed (the captcha).
3. Enter your **phone number**, then the **code sent to you via text** — so make sure you have that phone with you.
4. Type your **new password**, confirm it, and click **finish**.
5. Return to the portal and log in with your student email and the new password to confirm it worked.

Your new password must be at least **10 characters**, mix uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters, and must **not be any of your official names** — reusing your name is the usual reason a reset gets rejected.

## If you're still stuck

Tell me which system is failing and what the error message says, and I can be more precise. Two things I can't resolve from the documented procedures: if you never received the email containing your account details and password, or if the verification code never arrives on your phone, those need a human to fix — raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base):** "How to login to LMS" (LMS); "Reset your student portal password" (Knowledgebase); "Student Email / Mcampus Email / Corporate Email" (LMS). No direct article links were listed with these entries — the full Knowledge Base is at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

observations.question: Hi, I forgot my password and I am locked out. Please help.
observations.answer:
No worries — being locked out is stressful, but you can reset this yourself in a couple of minutes. Here's how to recover your **Student Portal** password:

1. Go to the student portal at **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and click **Forgot your password?** on the login screen.
2. Key in your **Amref student email address** and the **characters displayed** on screen (the character check is there to confirm a person, not a bot, is making the request).
3. Key in your **phone number**, then enter the **code sent to you by text** — this is how the system confirms it's really you before releasing the account.
4. Type in your **new password**, confirm it, and click **Finish**.
5. Go back to the portal and log in with your **student email and new password** to verify the reset worked.

When choosing the new password, it must meet these rules or it will be rejected:

- **Length:** at least 10 characters.
- **Complexity:** a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
- It must **not be any of your official names**.

One thing to expect afterwards: because you've just changed your password, the next sign-in will most likely prompt you for your **additional verification** — either a code from the **Microsoft Authenticator app** or one sent by text message. That's normal, not a sign that the reset failed. Verification is usually only requested the first time you sign in to a new app or device, or right after a password change, so keep your phone nearby for that first login.

A caveat: the steps above are the documented procedure for the **Student Portal**. If your lockout is actually on a different system — for example your university email or Moodle/LMS — that particular reset path isn't covered in the Help Desk articles I have, so please raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke and they'll unlock it for you. Also, if the text message with the code never arrives, the portal has no documented alternative route, so the Help Desk is the right next step there too.

The screenshots below show the sign-in and verification screens you'll be working with.

**Sources**
- Reset your student portal password — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase
- Setting up Microsoft Authenticator — Amref Help Desk Knowledgebase
- Help Desk: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke

observations.question: How do I use Microsoft Teams for my classes?
observations.answer:
Happy to walk you through this. Microsoft Teams is the collaboration platform you'll use for online meetings, classrooms, document sharing, and private or group chats — and your AMIU email account is the key that unlocks it.

**Getting into Teams**

1. **Have your AMIU-issued email credentials ready.** The email address the university gave you is what grants you access to the Microsoft Office Suite — Teams, Outlook (email), Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Stream, Forms, OneDrive, OneNote, To-Do, Visio, Whiteboard and Yammer all run off that one account.
2. **Install the Teams app on your device.** Download it from https://www.microsoft.com/en-ww/microsoft-teams/download-app and install it on your laptop, tablet or mobile phone. Installing it is the recommended route for classes, since you get the full meeting and chat experience on whichever device you have with you.
3. **Or use Teams in your browser instead.** If you'd rather not install anything, go to https://login.microsoft.com and access Teams from the web.
4. **Sign in with the email credentials you received from AMIU.** Use the same email address and password you use for your university email — there's no separate Teams account to create.
5. **Complete the extra verification step if you're prompted for it.** After you choose **Sign in**, Microsoft 365 may ask for more information to confirm it's really you:
   - Choose **Next**.
   - The default method is the free **Microsoft Authenticator** app. If it's already installed on your mobile device, select **Next** and follow the prompts to add this account.
   - If you don't have it installed, use the download link Microsoft provides on that screen, then continue with the prompts.
6. **Once you're in, start using it for your classes** — join or host online meetings, share documents with classmates and lecturers, chat privately or in groups, and work inside your class spaces.

The screenshots below show the sign-in screens you'll come across, so you can compare them with what's on your own device.

One thing to flag: how your lecturer adds you to a specific class team or shares a particular class meeting link isn't documented in the Help Desk material I have, so if you're signed in but can't see your class, please raise it with the Help Desk at https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke.

**Sources**
- LMS — Microsoft Teams (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base)
- Knowledgebase — Microsoft 365 additional verification / Microsoft Authenticator setup (Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base)
- Help Desk: https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke
